phoenix_chronicles.quest.phoenix_forge_t:
A §aGTCEU Modern§r pack focused on adding cool new machines and progression beyond base §bUHV§r. With a theme of §6reclamation of what once was lost§r, you'll journey through many tiers, starting by wading through §3LV§r and ultimately becoming a multiversal power in §5MAX§r voltage.

Be sure to check out the other sections of this quest page to learn §ehow to get started!§r

The early game is intended to be mostly §aeasy§r. To that end, rubber can be made like any other plate using hammers, and steam production has been §2significantly buffed§r.


---
phoenix_chronicles.quest.steam_changes.d:
The Steam Age progression has been simplified with easier recipes, and steam power has been significantly buffed!

All steam machines that generate steam now provide an additional §aboost to the millibuckets§r per process.

Introducing three new steam-powered machines: the §6Steam Foundry§r, the §6Steam Compressor§r, and the §6Steam Separator§r! These are perfect for powerful automation leveraging this enhanced steam output.


---



The new Steam Age tier material is §cFiery Bronze§r, crafted from a §e3:1:1§r ratio of §ecopper dust§r, §etin dust§r, and §cdormant ember dust§r to yield 4 §cFiery Bronze Dust§r, which can then be smelted into ingots.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.q_263fd1f608390: You awaken on a cold, hard floor, with a blazing headache.

Finding yourself within a vast temple dedicated to a phoenix, a familiar stirring takes hold. You discover a library and are drawn to a single book: the Flaming Records. Within its pages, schematics and plans of incredible machines awaken something within you. A section on "PhoenixWare?" reveals only, "Power beyond reality, created by P⍑𝙹ᒷリ╎ ̇/⍊╎リᒷ—once one of us, now something more." You feel like you should know who this is, but the name escapes you. With a sense of unanswered questions, you exit the temple into the blinding light.

The world outside bears the marks of a vibrant community now overgrown, littered with the fascinating wreckage of broken machines and automation that sparks an unexpected excitement.

This is not a story of invention, but of reclamation.

This is: §4§lPhoenix Forge Technologies§r§r

And you WILL get back what you lost.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.q_202f9b4c5659a: You shouldn't run out of power before you can recharge this in HV. But §ojust in case§r, submit yours here and receive a fully charged one in return!
phoenix_chronicles.quest.noob_traps.desc:
"§cNoob Traps§r" are early-game features or machines that appear helpful to new players but are inefficient or useless. Here are some examples:

§bHP Steam Macerator§r and §bHP Steam Furnace§r: These are significantly §4slower§r (over 150%!) than the multiblock §aSteam Grinder§r and §aSteam Oven§r. The §bHP Steam Macerator§r also requires §fSteel§r to craft.

§bLV Extruder§r: A classic noob trap as it has §4no functional recipes§r.


---



§bLV Equivalents of Steam Machines§r (excluding the Extractor): These run at the same slow speed as their HP Steam versions but are much more §cdifficult to acquire§r.

§eElectric Furnaces§r and §eElectric Alloy Smelters§r: While seemingly an upgrade, they are outclassed by the §6Multi-Smelter§r at §6HV§r. Until then, the §aSteam Oven§r and §bHP Steam Alloy Smelter§r are sufficient.

§dMV Macerator§r: Surprisingly §4slower§r than the early §aSteam Grinder§r and provides §4no bonus byproducts§r.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.tool_belt.title: Tool Belt
phoenix_chronicles.quest.tool_belt.subti: Take some weight off your inventory
phoenix_chronicles.quest.tool_belt.descr:
With your first §8Steel§r under your belt §7(ha!)§r, you can make a §bTool Belt§r to free up inventory space from all those pesky GT tools. It can be equipped in its own §ddedicated Curio slot§r.

By default, the hotkey to open the belt is §eR§r, but you can rebind it if you prefer. From this GUI, you can place tools inside the belt's storage, and swap them with your §dmain-hand tool§r whenever is convenient.

The belt has a small initial inventory of a single tool. This can be expanded by combining the belt with §bBelt Pouches§r in an §aAnvil§r - the maximum slottage is §69 slots§r.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.is_it_a_phantom: Is it a Phantom? Is it an Elytra?
No, it's Steve with a glider!

Once you have steel, you can make a Hang Glider. This might be a good item to grab before you hit up the §cNether§r.

If you don't have enough Leather yet, make a §9Butchering Knife§r and employ its inherent Looting III to hunt some cows.

---


§l§3Lore:§r§o The Hang Glider originally came from a mod known as OpenBlocks. As its utility was too great to be left on earlier versions, it was ported all the way up to modern versions.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.q_4dc49ae1e9c61: Not needed, but check them out anyways?

You've got to start somewhere, so why not right here? Seriously, check these out – it'll be worth your while!

While playing base GregTech Community Edition (GTCEu) is certainly possible, many modpacks enhance the experience with additional mods and recipes that make progression feel even more rewarding.
The §aIron Furnaces§r mod adds more furnaces to make smelting a little easier in the early game. While you won't be using these all the way through, they do add a nice touch as you begin your GregTech journey.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.furnace_mk1.des:
The §7Wrought Iron Furnace§r smelts in §a160 ticks§r.

That's roughly §b9 seconds§r, a noticeable §22-second§r improvement over a vanilla furnace!

Plus, it's quite cheap to craft, requiring just 8 §fwrought iron ingots§r around a standard furnace.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.furnace_mk_2.de:
The §esilver furnace§r is a direct upgrade to the §7wrought iron furnace§r.

It now smelts at §a140 ticks§r. Whoa, that's a whole §b1 second§r faster!

Plus, it's not too expensive, costing just 8 §fsilver ingots§r to craft.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.furnace_mk3.des:
Upgrading your §esilver furnace§r will reward you with this §6golden furnace§r, straight from Midas himself!

It now smelts at §a120 ticks§r, or §b6 seconds§r – now you're gaining some serious speed!

Grab some §egold§r from a magnetite vein and upgrade that bad boy. It takes 8 §egold ingots§r and a §esilver furnace§r.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.furnace_mk4.des:
Thought §6gold§r was strong enough? Not quite! Now it's time to upgrade to the §bdiamond furnace§r.

It smelts at a cool §a80 ticks§r, which is just §b5 seconds§r – your impatience will soon be quenched!

§3Diamonds§r should be fairly easy to find by now, but maybe hold off on ore processing them just yet, okay?
phoenix_chronicles.quest.furnace_mk5.des:
Hrrmmm, wait, you aren't a villager? My bad, continue on.

The §aemerald furnace§r and the §bcrystal furnace§r both smelt at a blazing §a40 ticks§r, or just §b2 seconds§r per item!

Now, §2emeralds§r are a bit trickier to acquire, requiring a venture into the §4§lNether§r. Alternatively, you can craft the §bcrystal furnace§r, but it needs an §5eye of ender§r, so the choice is yours. I won't be responsible for any... unforeseen consequences.

However, perhaps the speed is worth the effort? And keep in mind that crafting one of these furnaces is necessary to create the §0obsidian furnace§r.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.furnace_mk6.des:
This §0obsidian furnace§r cooks items at a blistering §a20 ticks§r each – that's just §bONE SECOND§r! This might be a tad insane, but you do need to progress through all the other furnaces to get here, so it's quite the achievement!

If you haven't crafted the §aemerald furnace§r/§bcrystal furnace§r and ventured into the §4§lNether§r for §6blaze rods§r, now's the time! Maybe even consider some upgrades for this beast? Please?
phoenix_chronicles.quest.furnace_mk7.des:
The pinnacle of single-block smelting before the ultimate smelting source!

The §bnetherite furnace§r smelts items in a mere §a5 ticks§r – that's a blazing §bquarter of a second§r per item!

And don't forget the §eFactory Upgrade§r! Smelting 5 items simultaneously at that speed means a staggering §a20 items processed per second§r!



---


However, it's now time to graduate to the §2§lMulti Smelter§r! Don't know what that is? The §2§lMulti Smelter§r is one of my favorite High Voltage (HV) multiblocks.

Yes, it's power-hungry, but its overclocking potential and the parallel processing from its coils are absolutely worth it. Don't believe me? Go build one yourself – you're welcome😊!
phoenix_chronicles.quest.power.title: Power!!!
phoenix_chronicles.quest.power.subtitle: Shocking, isnt it?
phoenix_chronicles.quest.power.descripti:
Everything kinda needs power to run. (This ofc does not apply to steam machines running with steam, unless you count it). Because of this, you have to learn to manage your power and store it.

Some fun things in the future include solar panels, thermal machines like the sterling dynamo, and at hv, Fission!!!
phoenix_chronicles.quest.q_2620df5043f6f:
Let's dive into the fascinating world of GregTech power, starting with §6EU (Energy Units)§r.

Now, the EU system operates quite differently from other power systems you might be familiar with. A crucial distinction is the §bvoltage tier system§r. §4BE WARNED§r: connecting higher voltage tier generators or dynamo hatches to lower tier infrastructure will result in §4CATASTROPHIC FAILURE – THINK EXPLOSIONS!§r

Conversely, §cNEVER§r connect an §2LV cable§r to an §3MV generator or machine§r. Doing so will overload and destroy the cable, leading to a frustrating waste of valuable resources.


---



§aGregTech wires§r serve as the conduits for transferring power between your energy generation and your EU-consuming machines. To establish a connection, simply §bShift + Right-Click§r a machine with the wire in hand, or utilize §9wire cutters§r. For enhanced efficiency and safety, you can wrap these wires with §eyellow rubber§r. This simple step slightly reduces power loss over longer distances and, importantly, prevents accidental §4electrocution§r.

A word of caution: §cAVOID§r standing on uncovered wires! The consequences are, well, §4shocking§r.

For long-distance power transmission without loss or personal risk, consider §aSuperconductors§r. These advanced wires eliminate energy loss entirely and boast a significantly higher §bampacity§r (current-carrying capacity) compared to their regular counterparts.


---



Speaking of transmission, let's address §cCable Loss§r. This is the gradual depletion of EU as power travels along a cable over distance (per wire block). While seemingly minor at first, it can become significant over long runs. Fortunately, progression unlocks more efficient cables and, eventually, §aSuperconductors§r, which eliminate this issue. In the early game, be mindful of loss and prioritize §aSuperconductors§r (use §b#superconductor§r in EMI to find them quickly!).


---



Now, let's delve into §eAmps and Converters§r.

§eAmps§r represent the number of energy packets at a specific voltage. Think of §evoltages§r as the size of the packets and §eamps§r as the quantity. §cNEVER§r use cables with a lower amperage rating than the power you're transmitting! Overloading cables causes them to overheat and burn out, potentially damaging their §eyellow rubber insulation§r.

§aConverters§r are vital for converting §2Forge Energy (FE)§r into §6EU§r, allowing integration of FE-producing machines into the GregTech power system. While they can also convert §6EU§r back to §2FE§r, using wires is generally more efficient for this native conversion (current ratio: §61 EU = 4 FE§r).


---



Finally, we have §bTransformers§r. These essential devices allow you to step up voltage tiers (e.g., multiple LV amps to higher MV packet strength), improving power efficiency over long distances. However, always remember: cable and wire amperage and voltage ratings must match the transmitted power! Failure to do so will result in a rather §4explosive§r situation.

phoenix_chronicles.quest.building_mulitb:
§bShift Right-Clicking§r a multiblock controller without anything in hand shows a §a3D preview§r of its structure. Doing the same while holding a §eTerminal§r will §2automatically build§r the multiblock.

§cImportant Tip for Terminal Building§r: Keep your input/output buses and hatches in your AE2 system (or other storage). The terminal builds based on the JEI preview, which might place your I/O in unwanted locations. Attach them after the multiblock is formed.

phoenix_chronicles.quest.q_53ca978eda44d:
In base §bae2§r, there are §achannels§r. §aChannels§r are directly correlated to the amount of §5me devices§r you can have on your network. For example each terminal would be it's own §achannel§r.

However, we have §bdecided§r to in favor of turning these §3channels off§r. §bWhy§r, you might ask? Well, the §6gregified ae2 componets§r are already pricey enough, where adding channels to that would be kinda mean.



---



If you want them back on, you can run the command /ae2 channelmode default, 2x, or 4x (infinite is the setting this pack uses.)

There are some who prefer the complexity of channels. I can't really blame them, so have at ye and have fun!

phoenix_chronicles.quest.all_the_process:
The core of GregTech progression lies in mastering intricate §bProcessing Lines§r. These are the industrial arteries of your base, transforming raw resources into advanced components.

This comprehensive section serves as your §aintegrated guide§r, focusing solely on the most §bcritical production chains§r. It provides essential information and starting points to help you navigate each major process.

§l§6It is time to process your world, and make it truly yours.§r§r
phoenix_chronicles.quest.clay_line.title: Clay Line
phoenix_chronicles.quest.clay_line.descr:
The §bElectrolyzer§r is a foundational machine for elemental separation. By processing §eClay Dust§r within it, you will obtain four crucial resources: §aLithium Dust, Sodium Dust, Silicon Dust,§r and §aAluminum Dust§r. Each plays a vital role in your industrial expansion.

* §a§lLithium:§r Your primary component for §dLV Batteries§r and a critical ingredient for many higher-tier energy storage solutions.
* §a§lSodium:§r Also used in §dBatteries§r (though less potent than Lithium), and crucial for advanced §dchemicals§r like Sodium Potassium and Sodium Sulfide, used in later §dplastics§r.
* §a§lSilicon:§r Fundamentally important for creating §dSilicon Boules§r and subsequently §dWafers§r, the basis of all integrated circuits. Also a versatile component in various §dalloys§r.
* §a§lAluminum:§r An indispensable metal for §dMV components, machines,§r and §dhulls§r. Due to its extensive use in §bAE2 systems§r, maintaining a significant §6stockpile§r of Aluminum is highly recommended.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.hnn_line.title: HNN Line
phoenix_chronicles.quest.hnn_line.descri:
Progress in this pack often requires specific §aMob Drops§r. The §bHostile Neural Networks§r system offers a controlled and automated solution, bypassing the need for traditional mob farms.

This powerful system consumes §cFlaming Prediction Matrixes§r to operate. You can craft these by combining §eClay Balls§r with a §cpiece of Flaming Dust§r.

§r§l§6Bonus Tip:§r Obtaining §ageneral predictions§r allows you to §aright-click§r them, granting valuable §aExperience Point§r!

If you want a clear showing of how this custom line works go here
Matrix Line
phoenix_chronicles.quest.q_0097649dfe924:
Enter the intricate world of §bPetrochemistry§r! This vast field transforms §oCarbon Compounds§r (like §eOil§r and §eWood Byproducts§r) into precise §aChemicals§r. These are vital for crafting everything from advanced §dPlastics§r to durable §dEpoxy Resins§r.

Your first breakthrough: producing §aEthylene§r. This essential building block will allow you to synthesize your first plastic: §aPolyethylene§r!

§r§l§6Pro Tip:§r Petrochemistry can feel overwhelming. Instead of exploring every oil's uses, §r§o§6focus on the recipes for the product you NEED.§r§o §6Build by demand!§r
phoenix_chronicles.quest.platline.title: PlatLine
phoenix_chronicles.quest.platline.descri:
The §bPlatinum Line§r is your dedicated process for extracting valuable precious metals from specialized ores. This complex chain begins by converting raw ores into §aRaw Platinum Group Sludge§r.

This §aSludge§r is then meticulously refined into essential products such as §bRuthenium§r, §bRhodium§r, and the highly valuable §bRarest Earth§r. §bRarest Earth§r undergoes further processing to yield crucial later-game metals: §dOsmium§r and §dIridium§r.

§6§o§lStrategic Tip:§r §bRuthenium§r is especially vital, required in large quantities for §bRTm Alloy Coils§r and numerous §bAssembly Line§r components. Due to this high demand, it is strongly advised to begin establishing your §bPlatinum Line§r production early.

The most efficient primary ore for this process is §eSheldonite§r, which is found in significant quantities alongside §eEnd veins of Platinum§r.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.naqline.title: NaqLine
phoenix_chronicles.quest.wetware.title: Wetware
phoenix_chronicles.quest.epoxy_line.desc:
§bEpoxy§r, a foundational polymer, is indispensable for §dCircuit Boards§r from §bLuV§r tier and upwards. Synthesize it by reacting §eBisphenol A§r with §eEpichlorohydrin§r in a §bChemical Reactor§r; these precursors involve advanced Petrochemistry.

phoenix_chronicles.quest.pipes.title: Pipes
phoenix_chronicles.quest.pipes.subtitle: Moving Fluids automaticly
phoenix_chronicles.quest.pipes.descripti:
Now, pipes are pretty simple. Just connect them to your machines, add a pump, and they'll move fluid.

Each pipe tier has tiny, small, normal, large, and huge variants with different fluid capacities. GregTech pipes have a system where specialized pipes move specific fluids.

For example, §6bronze pipes§r can't move acids, but §e gold pipes§r can. The early recommended progression is §6bronze§r -> §5potin§r -> §7steel§r. These will serve you well for a while.


---



Use a wrench on pipes for two things: 1) Lock flow direction (shift-right click with wrench and empty offhand) – great for large systems. 2) Manually connect/disconnect – useful for troubleshooting.

You can also use §bEnderIO fluid conduits§r to pull liquids without the fluid rules. Use an extraction upgrade for speed.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.q_614a47c0fd248:

§cIMPORTANT!§r Void sugarcane overflow! Use a Storage Void Upgrade in a drawer to prevent lag/corruption. Seriously, void it!
phoenix_chronicles.quest.q_3ac1e101ef831:
The §bSteam Foundry§r is a machine that uses the §dpressure of steam§r to alloy useful materials into more complex forms. With the high need for steel, this machine will make that process much less painful.

Furthermore, with the innate §aparallel processing§r that all steam-using multiblocks have, it is §afaster than 12 LV alloy smelters§r.


---


"Needing a way to create alloys on a more industrial scale you decide to continue this trend of steam. You create a method of §b§lsuperheating§r steam, then using that steam to superheat alloys through heat transference and melt them allowing them to merge and form a new material. A §a§lstronger§r more §d§ldurable§r alloy.

Using an bronze base you make the steam transfer into a chamber outputting heat on the bronze base that is designed to withstand temperatures upwards of §425,000 Kelvin§r. This base allows the metals to melt and fuse to make alloys."
phoenix_chronicles.quest.steam_power.des:
You might already be familiar with EU as the Energy Unit for Electric machines - but what about Steam?

Steam machines will run using a proportional amount of steam at a 1:1 ratio of EU to Steam as listed in your recipe viewer of choice.

---


After each recipe, the Steam machines will vent cooler steam (with snazzy particles) from the side with the square. This is the exhaust port.

Important: Keep the exhaust port unblocked - this is neither an input nor an output slot! If the machine fails to vent steam, it will stop working.

Reminder: Use your Wrench to change which side the exhaust port is facing (right-click).

---


Regular Steam Machines are twice as slow to complete recipes as is listed in EMI. To bring your machines up to speed, you may want to pursue High Pressure Steam machinery.

High Pressure Steam Machines are the same speed as indicated by EMI, but with adjusted steam consumption. You will unlock them once you obtain Steel.

---


Psst! If you're not in a Hardcore world, we invite you to stand on top of pipes transporting steam, or stand right in front of the vent as the machines are running recipes.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.electricity.des:
You have likely realised by now that the Energy system in §2GregTech§r is §cnowhere near as simple§r as the §1RF§r you may be used to using in modded Minecraft.

The energy unit of GregTech is the EU.

§1EU§r mechanics have a certain flair to them, and are not dissimilar to real-world electricity. They can also be §4dangerous and punishing§r if mishandled. However, the power system gives GregTech players a lot of §6satisfaction§r when harnessed well.

§l§3Lore:§r§o The Amperage bug, exploit or feature (call it whatever you want!) from 1.12.2 GTCE has been §lfixed§r§o in GTCEu. The Energy network now works as intended.

---


Let's go over some basic physics:

° §9Power§r = §2Voltage§r * §dAmperage§r
° §1Energy§r = §9Power§r * §6Time§r

§8Resistance§r is an excluded concept in GregTech, instead being partially simulated as cable loss.

The units are defined as such:

- §1EU§r is the unit of §1Energy§r.
- §9EU/t§r is the §9Power§r.
- §dA§r or §dAmp§r is the §dAmperage§r.
- §2V§r §owould§r be the §2Voltage§r, but we prefer referring to it as §7LV§r, §bMV§r, §6HV§r... as those are the relevant values for gameplay (technically: §7LV§r = 32V = 32EU/t/A).

---


Electricity in GregTech travels in "packets". The size of each packet is equivalent to the voltage of its tier.

Taking an LV packet as an example, this "packet" would carry 32EU. Multiple blocks are capable of producing these EU packets, and packets are only produced if they are able to access a destination.

---


Every §6tick§r, §1EU§r §apackets§r attempt to transfer themselves from Energy Producers to Consumers. These §apackets§r have two parameters: a §2Voltage§r tier determined by the tier of the Producer, and §dAmperage§r. This determines how much §9Power§r can actually be transferred.

There are no partial Amps, meaning Energy is transferred only if the full Amp §apacket§r can be received. You might notice this from your machines sitting just below full EU capacity - they will only accept EU when they are missing at least 1A of their input voltage.

---


If a §3Machine§r receives a §2higher Voltage§r than its Tier, it'll §cexplode§r. Kaboom! Any excess §dAmperage§r won't have an adverse affect, as machines only consume as they need.

The machine explosion would usually also damage terrain, but we have disabled that feature in this pack.

---


In summary, Energy is transported in §apackets§r of §132EU§r for §7LV§r, §1128EU§r for §bMV§r... so on and so forth. The amount of energy that is actually received by a machine can end up being lower than energy sent, due to cable loss.

Machine Energy Input is limited by §2Voltage§r (too high and, well, §6boom§r!), and by §dAmperage§r. Thus, a §bMV§r Machine with §d2A§r Input connected to a §7LV§r line will never accept more than §964EU/t§r.

It is still possible to run §bMV§r Machines on §7LV§r lines, but only if the recipes are low enough §9Power§r, or if you have a §3MV Battery§r in the charging slot. The machine will only accept §d1A§r when idle, and so the §3Battery§r will recharge at a maximum rate of §932EU/t§r.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.q_0f2a7f519b3c6:
Transporting EU is done via direct connection, using §aWires§r or §aCables§r.

Wires are the inferior option as they will §celectrocute§r you and §close more energy§r as the electricity travels through the wire, so you want to use insulated Cables. Keep in mind that you can't combine cables into thicker variants, so make sure you insulate the right thickness to avoid any headaches.

§cCable loss§r means you will have to stick your Machines close to your Generators, but that will only be a problem in earlygame. If you peek through the quest book, you will eventually be able to obtain §6Superconductors§r, sidestepping this issue!

---


Keep in mind that GregTech cables suffer from "cable loss". Every block of cable that an EU packet travels will decrease its stored EU.

For instance, transferring §7LV§r current along 6 cables each with a loss of 5 EU/t will result in the packets arriving at their destination with a meagre 2 EU/t (32 - [6*5]). For this reason, you will want to keep your cables short until you can start to consider better alternatives.

---


§6Superconductors§r are special Wires available for each Voltage tier. They don't have any Cable counterpart, but that isn't necessary, as they have absolutely §6zero cable loss§r! They also don't damage you when you touch them.

They are the best choice for wiring at any tier, if not a little expensive in comparison to the other wires.

---


GT6-style Cables are §denabled§r. It means that placing Cables will only connect them to the block they were placed against. To open more connections, use your §5Wire Cutter§r on the grid.

---


§2GTCEu§r Cables now have §6native RF support§r! You can plug any RF appliance into an EU source and it will automatically convert. The ratio is §a4 : 1§r (RF : EU). Not that you can produce RF in this pack - but it's a thought if you wanted to make your own!
phoenix_chronicles.quest.q_2be355672e638:
The quantity of 1 packet per tick is known as an Amp (1A for short).

Each single-block Generator in GregTech is configured to produce §91A§r of its voltage tier. For §7LV§r, that results in §232EU/t§r.

If a machine requires 16EU/t, one "packet" of 32EU is sent §6every other tick§r (assuming no cable loss) - no more, no less.

A Battery Buffer with §94§r Batteries can produce up to §94 Amps§r for §2128EU/t§r as §7LV§r power, which is important for the §3Electric Blast Furnace§r - or to run multiple machines simultaneously.

Generic machines are configured to draw up to §92 Amps§r to account for cable loss. Other machines have specific §9Amps IN§r, which is described in their tooltip.

---


The most critical thing to know is that §acables§r have an §9Amperage §climit§r. Attempting to transport more Amps than this limit will §4burn your cable up§r.

§9Amps§r are drawn §oonly§r through the §aCables§r connecting the Producers and Consumers directly, and only drawn if the Consumers are active.

This means you can safely step down your Cables in certain places - feel free to experiment!
phoenix_chronicles.quest.q_54de75e97153e:
Why does every machine have a million variants across each tier? We'll let you in on an industry secret - overclocking is one of the main reasons.

Overclocking is a mechanic that happens when you try to run a recipe in a machine §dthat is higher tier than the recipe itself.§r The recipe will use an increased amount of energy, but the recipe time will be cut based on how many tiers you're overclocking by.

§l§3Lore:§r§o GTCE overclocking was extremely awkward. If the recipe consumed 16EU/t or below, it would do a classic 2.0x overclock. However if the recipe consumed more than 16EU/t, every Overclock would be 2.8x faster! GTCEu has a config to select the Overclock speed bonus.

---


A pro tip - for automated setups, overclock as little as possible!

Machines have a side menu to set the maximum voltage tier it will overclock to. Click on it to cycle through all the available Voltages and choose a limit.

---


Each tier above the recipe tier allows one overclock. Each overclock implies:

§9-§r §a2x§r recipe speed
§9-§r §a4x§r power consumption
§9->§r §c2x§r total energy cost

As you can see, there are upsides and downsides. It is a game of balance: ask yourself if you want faster recipes at the cost of greater power consumption.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.q_1647e0c649e21:
There are two really important factors to know when building Multiblocks.

Check EMI, and remember to keep things versatile.

---


Rule number one - check EMI!

This one was probably obvious, but EMI is so much more than just a cute picture of how the Multiblock looks when built! Use your mouse to §drotate§r the preview, and §9hover over the blocks used§r to view any extra information.

The EMI page also contains an ingredient list of required blocks. You can also §dright-click§r a block in the preview to get a display of all blocks that work in that specific position.

---


Rule number two - multiblocks are versatile!

There is no "definite" way to form the Multiblock. Most of the time, you have complete freedom over the §9tier of Buses/Hatches§r used - and you also have the ability to§d choose where you want your inputs/outputs§r.

Taking the EBF as an example, any tier of Energy/Bus/Hatch can be used, and they can be placed anywhere in place of a casing. Fluid Hatches are also optional, though you probably want them if you need to handle recipes involving fluid.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.troubleshooting: It's not forming? We've all been there before.

§9-§r If the recipe isn't happening, check if the Multiblock is properly plugged in (we all make these mistakes!).

§9-§r Remember to always perform the initial Maintenance "routine" at the appropriate hatch.

§9-§r Verify the recipe's EU/t usage - the max EU/t provided to the multiblock has to be greater than that of the recipe.

---


§9- §rCheck the special requirements the recipe may have (EMI always has some kind of indication if this is the case). Do you need to be in a Cleanroom, for example?

§9-§r Make sure the correct items are input into the buses/hatches. This is less obvious than in a regular machine, because you have to juggle between the Input Bus and Input Hatch.

§9-§r Make sure there is space for an output. Maybe the multiblock formed, but you forgot a Hatch. The other biggest offender is the Output Hatches being too low tier and thus having too little capacity - this trips people up with the Greenhouse!
phoenix_chronicles.quest.maintenance_hat:
Maintenance in GregTech is not as bad as you think (promise!), and adding a Maintenance Hatch to your multiblocks makes them look pretty industrial!

---


Most Multiblocks require a §3Maintenance Hatch§r. You will need to perform Maintenance for the Multiblock to begin operating.

This is done by having a §9Wrench§r, a §9Screwdriver§r, a §9Soft Mallet§r, a §9Hammer§r, a §9Wire Cutter§r, and a §9Crowbar§r in your inventory, opening the Maintenance Hatch and §eclicking the center spot once§r. §cThere's no need to move tools individually§r.

---


Alternatively, you can circumvent these problems by placing a §9Tape§r in the Maintenance Hatch, but a lot of people would jump at the chance to tell you that Tape is §o"unethical"§r - plus, tape is gated behind some polymers starting from §bMV§r.

---


Maintenance problems have a §d5%§r chance of occuring every §dhour of multiblock activity§r. Needless to say, they are §6very§r rare. Each maintenance problem increases the recipe duration by §c10%§r. Fixing these problems is done the same way as above.

At §6HV§r, you'll unlock other Maintenance Hatches that do not require manual repairs.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.q_6c8789a7b8946:
The §3Electric Blast Furnace§r, §3Pyrolyse Oven, §b§aMulti Smelter§r, and §3Cracking Unit§r all require Heating Coils. But why should you bother upgrading to higher tiers of Coil?

Coil progression can be viewed in the Milestones tab.

---


For the EBF, things get slightly complicated. The EBF smelts items at a certain §dtemperature§r. This is mainly determined by the tier of heating coil used - §r§6Cupronickel§r smelts at §d1800K§r, §bKanthal§r at §d2700K§r, etc. Additionally, starting from §6HV§r, each tier of energy adds §d100K§r to the temperature.

---


How does this affect you? Each EBF recipe has a certain base temperature. For example, §bAluminium§r is smelted at §d1700K§r. If the EBF temperature is not high enough, the recipe won't happen. If the EBF temperature is high enough, 2 different bonuses are applied:

§9-§r For every §d900K§r above the recipe temperature, the amount of energy required is multiplied by §a0.95x§r - which stacks.
§9-§r For every §d1800K§r above the recipe temperature, a single additional overclock will be §6100% efficient§r; in other words, it will §5quadruple the recipe speed§r, instead of doubling it.

---


The Pyrolyse Oven is much more simple in comparison to the EBF.

Cupronickel coils apply a §c+25% penalty§r to recipe duration - effectively, recipes are slower than listed if one uses Cupronickel coils.

Kanthal coils restore recipe duration to a regular length of time.

However, coils above Kanthal apply an §aadditive -50% bonus§r to recipe duration!

---


The Cracker is much more simple.

Every coil tier post-Cupronickel will reduce its energy usage by 10%.

Coils in the Multi Smelter reduce the amount of energy per operation whilst also increasing the number of items that can be processed in parallel.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.muffler_hatches:
The §3Electric Blast Furnace§r requires a §3Muffler Hatch§r to run. This hatch must be §cunobstructed§r so it can output its beautiful smoke particles.

§l§3Lore:§r§o In GregTech 5, polluting multiblocks had Muffler Hatches. The higher tier the hatch, the lower the Pollution output.

§oPollution had... interesting... effects, such as turning grass and dirt into sand.

---


When a recipe is performed, there is a small chance for the §3Muffler Hatch§r to give bonus items - typically tiny Dusts of Ash. These items can be processed for some helpful resources.

---


Do §onot§r try to automate the extraction of items from the §3Muffler Hatch§r! It's not intended to be an automation challenge, as it voids excess contents when full, so don't worry about it stopping machines from running.

Muffler Hatches in GTCEu are more about pure aesthetic (c'mon, you can't deny that those particles look good!) and small rewards, rather than punishing game mechanics.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.powering_multib:
Multiblocks do not look at the voltage of recipes when trying to craft. Instead, they simply check if they are being provided with enough Power.

§9Note:§r Be wary of Cable §closses§r bringing the actual power input below the recipe requirement! We §lhighly§r recommend either placing your §3Battery Buffer§r next to the §3Energy Hatches§r for the minimum cable length, or looking around this questbook to see if there are better alternatives to Cables.

---


The EBF needs a minimum of §4120EU/t§r power input to run its recipes. This can be achieved with §3two LV Energy Hatches§r. Each one takes 2 Amps of LV, so that's 4 Amps of LV for 128EU/t maximum power.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.multiblock_io.d:
Similarly to the Steam Multiblocks - hopefully, you made these! - you're going to need some §3Buses§r if you want to move items in and out.

For fluids, you'll instead need §3Hatches§r. Higher tiers of §3Hatches/Buses§r have more slots.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.all_about_the_c:
First off, be sure to check the §9tooltip§r - there's a lot of information in there!

Don't forget the §3Maintenance Hatch§r. If the structure refuses to form, rotate or replace the Controller, it can be a bit finicky. Don't worry - it doesn't have to be cube-shaped.

The Controller always has to be in the center. The rest of the top layer has to be §dFilter Casings§r.

All edges have to be §dPlascrete§r, and the sides can be §dCleanroom Glass§r.

Placing §3Generators§r or §3Mufflers§r inside is §cnot allowed§r. They're too dirty, so the Cleanroom will unform.

---


Upon assembly, the Cleanroom starts §4contaminated§r. While contamined, contained machines will not be able to operate.

The Cleanroom will drain 30 EU/t and slowly increase the cleanliness until its cleanliness is at 100%.

Once §9Clean§r, recipes can run. At that point it will only draw 4EU/t. Keep it powered at all times or it will get dirty again!

The bigger the Cleanroom, the longer it takes to become Clean.

§9Note§r: When the time comes, Multiblocks must also be put into Cleanrooms in order to run cleanroom recipes!

---


Need to transfer EU? Try using §3Hulls§r or §3Diodes§r.

Item and Fluid transfer can be done using §3Passthrough Hatches§r.

§3Machine Hulls§r can also "double" as §6ME Cables§r to extend your ME Network inside your Cleanroom.

If you used any §dDoor(s)§r in the structure, they can remain open. Not very realistic, but convenient!

---


§9§eConfigs:§r If you dislike the Cleanroom mechanics, it can be toggled off in the config file with §5"B:enableCleanroom"§r. Multiblocks can be made to ignore cleanroom requirements with §5"B:cleanMultiblocks"§r. We encourage you to try it out before deciding.

---


In the real world, a Cleanroom is a well-isolated room which maintains a very low concentration of dust and airborne particles. They're normally used for scientific research, and in real-life semiconductor manufacturing. Clean rooms are specifically designed to keep out as many airborne particulates as can be.

Clean rooms are also sometimes used with the purpose of preventing materials from escaping! This is often the primary aim in fields such as pharmaceutics, nuclear work, and hazardous biology.

The more you know!
phoenix_chronicles.quest.understanding_t:
There are many ways to automate Ordered Items: GT item pipes, Redstone, other mods, you name it! This quest will attempt to guide you through a setup using §3AE2§r.

Have the Pattern Provider face an §3Item P2P§r. Set two output P2Ps: one into the first §3Input Bus§r, and the other into §3Item Pipes§r. Make your Item Pipes connect to all Input Buses including the first. Don't forget §dBlocking Mode§r!

With this setup, assembly items should be fully automated!

---


Whilst item automation was relatively simple, fluid automation is slightly harder.

Fluid Pipes behave differently compared to Item Pipes, so you §4won't§r be able to use the same solution as above.

This quest won't explain how to do this entirely §7(due to it being off by default)§r, so the full solution is left as an exercise to the reader.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.q_6da28f169ced9:
Scanning is the first step for research. Take the item shown in EMI and put it with a §3Data Stick§r to scan it. This will §4consume§r the item and put Data on the Data Stick. Pretty straightforward, right?

You will need at least an §6HV Scanner§r to progress to §dLuV§r, an §5EV Scanner§r for §aLuV Energy Hatches§r, and an §1IV Scanner§r for §aFusion Reactors§r.

---


Later on, recipes will require different §aData Storage Items§r for research, such as the §3Data Orb§r. This process will remain the same, but will use different Data Storage Items instead. They can also be copied the same way, but you cannot copy between different types of storage items.

---


Eventually, you'll want multiple Assembly Lines, but you won't want to re-scan for every Research. This is why you can also use the §3Scanner§r to §dCopy Data§r. Place the data stick you want to copy in one slot, and a blank one in the other. This will copy the contents of the first stick into the second!

§4Important§r: Using two different data sticks with data on them will cause one to §4overwrite§r the other. Be careful!
phoenix_chronicles.quest.q_1366981bd8cd9:
§aRotors§r have a §9Power§r, §dEfficiency§r and §4Durability§r that are based on tool stats.

§9Power§r is a multiplier applied to the production of the §3Turbine§r. This stacks multiplicatively with the §3Rotor Holder§r.

§dEfficiency§r reduces its fuel consumption. This again stacks multiplicatively with the §3Rotor Holder§r.

§4Durability§r is the lifetime of the §aRotor§r in seconds, when the §3Turbine§r§r is active.

---


§3Rotor Holders§r above the tier of the §3Large Turbine§r will multiplicatively §6double§r the production for every tier, whilst additively increasing the efficiency by 10% every tier.

---


§lSome pros of Large Turbines:

§9-§r Turbines can scale §9Power§r production far, far higher than their base output, thanks to tiered §3Rotor Holders§r.

§9-§r The §aRotor§r can give a huge boost to §dFuel efficiency§r and §9Power§r production.

§9-§r You get a lot of satisfaction for setting them up properly (yay!)

---


§l...and some cons of Large Turbines:

§9-§r Turbines work off §eInertia§r, which requires them to continuously run to achieve maximum Power.

§9-§r Any excess Energy produced will be §cvoided§r. You will §lneed§r to use large Energy Buffers and an §3Advanced Energy Detector§r if you wish to stay efficient.

§9-§r They require a §aRotor§r, which will lose durability over time and eventually §cbreak§r.

§9-§r A little bit of Math is required to get the expected results.

---


A Turbine's §9Power§r output affects both the fuel consumption and the EU/t generation. It is calculated with the following formula:

§eproduction = baseEUt x rotorPower x 2^(rotorHolderTier - turbineTier)§r

The §dEfficiency§r reduces fuel consumption, but does not alter the EU/t generation. It is calculated with the following formula:

§eefficiency = rotorEfficiency x (1 + 0.1 x (rotorHolderTier - turbineTier))§r

---


Let's simulate a Large Steam Turbine, with an Ultimet Rotor and an §5EV§r Rotor Holder:

Production = 1024 x 1.60 x 2 = 3276 EU/t

Efficiency = 1.30 x 1.10 = 143%

(Therefore, steam consumption would be 4582 L/t - this is above a Titanium Boiler, or a Tungstensteel Boiler with ~70% throttle)

---


Next, we'll analyse the Gas Turbine, with a Chrome Rotor and an §5EV§r Rotor Holder:

Production = 4096 x 1.70 x 1 = 5325 EU/t

Efficiency = 1.55 x 1.00 = 155%

(The same fuel consumption would produce 3435 EU/t using 6.7 Turbo Gas Turbines!)

---


Finally, how about we check out the Plasma Turbine, with a HSS-S Rotor and a §cZPM§r Rotor Holder:

Production = 16834 x 2.50 x 4 = 168340 EU/t

Efficiency = 1.80 x 1.20 = 216%

(This is more than a ZPM Amp!)
phoenix_chronicles.quest.q_57de7059d524f:
Simply put, Gregicality Multiblocks are larger versions of the GregTech machines you might be familiar with. The obvious increase in resource cost is worth your time, as they can be upgraded to gain the ability to process recipes in parallel.

---


They also introduce Machine Modes - depending on the configured machine mode, the Multiblock will use a different recipe type when processing materials. You can change this from the machine GUI by clicking on the Robot Arm button.

---


By including Parallel Control Hatches in your Gregicality Multiblocks, you can grant them parallel processing capability. There are 4 tiers of hatch, each further increasing parallel capability by an factor of 4.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.parallelization:
§lWhy go parallel?

§9-§r §4Parallelization is superior§r to overclocking! Take advantage of this for your passive setups such as Ore Processing or Oil Distilling.

§9-§r §6Distinct buses§r: §3GCYM Machinery§r can accept multiple §3Input Buses§r. Use it for your pattern automation with §3Extruder§r, §3Engraver§r, and many other.

Power cost is based on the current recipe being run, times the number of §4parallel§r being performed.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.beginner_ore_pr:
§lWhy process ore?

The main purpose of GregTech Ore Processing is to provide §abyproducts§r on top of the initial outcome. At Steam Age, none of the byproducts are obtainable, but this will become relevant soon.

---


§lHow should I start?

The steps available in the Steam Age go as follows:

One Ore (block) §9->§r Two Crushed Ores (Macerator)

One Crushed Ore §9->§r One Impure Dust (Hammer)

One Impure Dust §9->§r One Dust (In world crafting)

One Dust §9->§r One Ingot (Furnace, you should know this one)

---


A pickaxe or mining hammer enchanted with Hammering, or a GregTech Hammer directly, gives Crushed Ores from breaking Ore blocks, but only at a 1:1 ratio.

Silk Touch is essential to obtain an ore block - this pack includes a recipe for the book.

---


The rule bends for ores giving more than two dusts (such as §cRedstone§r), and for dusts that cannot be smelted (§cRedstone§r... again!).

However, you can still smelt the ore directly to get §9half the amount§r you would from the full processing.

---


§dEMI does not indicate Impure Dust to Clean Dust conversion§r, so keep that in mind that you can §athrow them into filled cauldrons§r.

---


Take this reward for listening to us waffle on WITHOUT nodding off!
phoenix_chronicles.quest.q_7fcfe4c40837c: Extracting an ore's full potential... at last!

A shopping list for anyone looking to automate §6Ore Processing§r on a large scale:

§9-§r One or more §3IV Macerators§r (the higher the tier, the higher your chances of byproducts!).
§9-§r The §3Large Centrifuge§r. Set it to work as a Thermal Centrifuge, and you're off to the races.
§9-§r One or more §3MV Electrolyzers§r - you could possibly make the large version if there's enough demand.
§9-§r A §3Multi Smelter§r.
§9-§r A §3Packager§r of any tier for those pesky Small/Tiny Dusts (think Rare Earth!)
§9-§r Inventories acting as a large buffer, such as §3Tungstensteel Crates§r.
§9-§r §3ME Storage Buses§r, or a lot of §3Item Pipes§r + §aFilter covers§r, or §aItem Tag Filters§r.

---


What you may §ealso want to§r add:

§9-§r A few §3LV Ore Washers§r for quick washing purposes.
§9-§r Alternately, a §3Large Ore Washer§r, accompanied with a set of §3Distilleries§r for §dDistilled Water§r.
§9-§r A second §3Large Centrifuge§r... this time set to Centrifuge mode for impure/purified dusts.
§9-§r §3Chemical Baths§r for the special Byproducts that require §dMercury§r or §dSodium Persulfate§r to obtain.
§9-§r §3Sifters§r of any tier (higher tier = better chanced output), for gem ores.
§9-§r §3Electromagnetic Separators§r.

---


If the Large Machines aren't your thing, you could always try using tons of §7LV§r machinery, and route with some clever piping.

Overclocking is §cnot§r energy efficient, which is why it is generally better to go for §6low-tier machines§r in §3passive setups§r. One could also argue they are cheaper.

In previous versions of GregTech, you could just use §3Processing Arrays§r, as they could condense many low-tier machines down into a §asingle speedy multiblock§r. Players desiring §esimilar processing speeds§r nowadays should really look to the §bGCYM machinery§r - it's quick, easy to upgrade when you tier up (§dEnergy Hatches§r are usually cheaper than 16 low-tier machines!), and c'mon now... they just look really cool.

---


§o§7"Should I go for the optional byproducts?"

Yes.

However, the "routes" you take your ores through processing is up to you. Want to macerate twice because you prefer the other byproducts? Go ahead!

Note that §3Thermal Centrifuging§r is usually a good idea, as doing so unlocks a §6unique Byproduct§r from the maceration step.

---


Chalcopyrite, Chalcocite, Bornite, Tetrahedrite, Pentlandite and Sheldonite ores should all be turned into their §dPurified Crushed§r variants and sent to your §6Platinum Group Metal§r chain.

Purified Crushed Galena/Sphalerite should be reserved for Indium until you set up the Naquadah line. At that point, you'll have more Indium than you'll ever need.

§aGallium§r, §aChrome§r, §aNiobium§r, §aRare Earths§r, and §aGlowstone§r are all §6Byproducts§r you might want to prioritise.

If you think we're missing any pertinent products, hit us up on Discord, and we'll be sure to add your favourites to this list.

---


As you've probably realised, Applied Energistics 2 will be very, very helpful when automating all of this.

§3ME Storage Buses§r are very powerful for routing items when they enter your ME network. They also have a huge whitelist or blacklist configuration. Attach them to some §3Tungstensteel Crates§r to buffer intermediate items, or use a dedicated AE2 subnet.

To combine §aSmall Dusts§r into full §aDusts§r, you'll want a §3Storage Bus§r on high priority paired with an §dItem Tag§r filter set to §e§ldusts/small§r. Note that Small Dusts may be used for Boules, and a few Tiny Dusts are needed for the PBI chain, so you can blacklist them from the filter if you desire.

---


For ores that you want to process quickly but don't care for the Byproducts as the full "route" would take too long in the machines, prioritize filtering them for quick washing.

The typically "best" path is: Macerator -> Ore Washing -> Thermal Centrifuge -> Macerator. If you deviate from it for various reasons, you're gonna have to set filters §emanually§r. Gasp!

phoenix_chronicles.quest.cover_behaviour: Extra utility without taking up blockspace!

Almost any machine can have a cover on one of its faces, even if the machine would have no way to use said cover.

Opening a Cover is done by sneak right clicking with an §5empty hand§r. You can also right-click with a §5Screwdriver§r, or sneak-right-click on another face using the grid.

---


For Covers that transfer Items/Fluids, you will have a button to enable/disable other forms of transfer through the cover:

§9- §rDisabled: only the cover will be allowed to transfer on this machine side.

§9-§r Allow Filtered (only relevant with a filter!): other transfer will be enabled only if it matches the filter

§9-§r Allow Unfiltered: any other transfer is allowed on this machine side.

Placing a cover of a lower voltage tier on a machine is §9safe§r.
phoenix_chronicles.task.cover_behaviour_: I'm an expert on Covers now, don't you worry.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.machine_autoout:
All machines typically have one §7Front Face§r, and one §9Output Face§r.

The §7Front Face§r should be obvious.\nThe §9Output Face§r is the face with a dot or hole on it. By default, this is at the back of the machine as you place it.

Machines can §aauto-output§r through their output face. To enable auto-output, click the appropriate button in the GUI. Fluid and item auto-outputs are toggled separately. Further control over auto-outputs can be achieved with §dFilters§r and §dCovers§r, which are explained in the quest to the upper left of this one.

---


Right-clicking a machine with a §5Wrench§r changes the output side, and shift-right-clicking changes the front side. Keep in mind that the front side §ccannot§r also be the output side!

By default, items and fluids cannot be inserted through the output side, but this can be toggled with a §5Screwdriver§r. Either right-click the output face directly, or shift-right-click on the grid corresponding to the side of the output.

There are unique machines that do not process recipes, such as the §3Pump§r, §3Miner§r, §3Fisher§r, §3Item Collector§r, etc. These machines will output on their §7Front Face§r (which is still marked as a dot).
The Wiremill lets you make §6two Wires or 8 Fine Wires from one Ingot§r from one Ingot. That should be three times cheaper than what you were doing up until now!

To the right of this quest are more lv machines to make your resources cost quite a bit less!



---


§9Note:§r Recipes inside §3LV Machines§r go up to a maximum usage of §a32 EU/t (LV)§r. Anything higher than that and you will need a §bMV§r (or better) Machine. Needless to say, we aren't quite there yet.

You need a Programmed Circuit to run some recipes, so if you don't want to use your precious lv circuits to make them I suggest to look at the quest below this one to learn what ghost circuits are.

Once you make this machine, your foray into the electric world will truly begin!

phoenix_chronicles.quest.lv_superconduct: We aren't losing a single Amp more

§6Superconductors§r are special Wires available for each Voltage tier. They don't come with a Cable counterpart, but that isn't necessary, as they have absolutely §6zero cable loss§r.

They also won't electrocute you when you step on them. This makes them the §6best§r choice for wiring, if not a little expensive in comparison to the other wires. (Also, a §oslight§r note here. §aAll§r custom §bsuperconductors§r can be smelted in a furnace. No need to worry about ebf times!)

If this did not already excite you, the 1x wire can support up to 2 amps!

phoenix_chronicles.quest.batteries.title: Batteries!
phoenix_chronicles.quest.batteries.descr:
§aBatteries§r can be put into the energy slot at the bottom middle of machine GUIs, or in a §3Battery Buffer§r.

When inside your inventory, they can be sneak-right-clicked to allow the batteries to §dcharge§r your EU items.

§7LV§r, §bMV§r, and §6HV§r Batteries come in three forms, allowing you to pick the one you find the best depending on materials you have. §dLithium§r has the best capacity, followed by §dCadmium§r, then §dSodium§r.

Our recommendation? Find a Salt vein, and either §aelectrolyze Salt§r for §dSodium§r, or §awash crushed Lepidolite§r for §dLithium§r.

Get §eany§r §aBattery§r to complete this quest.
By itself, the Battery Buffer does nothing. However, if you place batteries inside its internal storage, it will act as a power buffer.

The §3Battery Buffer§r handles §9two Amps in§r, and §9one Amp out§r, §dper Battery§r. The output side has the dot, and all other sides are used as inputs.

§6It'll also charge §lboth§r EU and RF Tools inside it§r.

This is a must have if you don't have unlimited power at hand. Get §eany§r §7LV§r Battery Buffer to finish the quest. However, the 16 slots variant is likely overkill at this stage.

---


§9Note:§r Don't loop your lossy Cables back to your Battery Buffer! If you think about it, you'll just end up voiding energy.

§l§3Lore:§r§o To be frank with you, the GTCE Battery Buffer was... mediocre. It's been reworked in GTCEu to provide a mix between GT5 and GTCE's functionality. Energy now splits evenly across all batteries!
phoenix_chronicles.quest.q_1e9be8d3f8a60:
This Quest explains the core mechanic of the §3Electric Blast Furnace§r, whilst the quest below will explore the mechanics of the Multiblock Parts that you'll also need. Be sure to refer to them.

Anyway, the §3EBF§r is your §efirst electric multiblock§r! Congrats. It's used to process materials at high temperatures.

You'll become familiar with the EBF to make §aAluminFrost§r and progress to §d§bMV Age§r. It can also make §7Steel§r faster than a alloy smelter.

---


It's important to keep in mind that the EBF is a beefy boy. The minimum power cost to run a recipe is §9120 EU/t§r! That's slightly under 4 §7LV§r Generators. This is why it was locked behind the Battery Quest. You may wish to consider building a separate power line, with separate Generators and Battery Buffer to run this.

phoenix_chronicles.quest.sapphire.descri:

§9§lA footnote:§r There's no way we could document all of the renewable routes in §bGregTech§r. This quest page merely serves as a primer to lead §6newer players§r through their options. Not every option listed in this quest book is optimal, so we urge you to experiment!
phoenix_chronicles.quest.q_55d8e30978cbb: More like game breaking, am I right?

Ah, the Rock Crusher - such an unassuming machine that initially appears to only really be a builder's best friend. Who could look past infinite Cobblestone, Deepslate, or Obsidian?

Don't be fooled, though, as this little machine might just shock you with the array of materials it makes renewable when you macerate its rocks down to dust form. The surrounding quests will clue you in.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.the_joy_of_cobb: Oh, we're only just getting started.
Cobblestone is just the start of things. Let's make a Cobbleworks!
phoenix_chronicles.quest.q_668a8bddee178:
§6Stone Dust§r can be centrifuged in §bMV§r for a wide range of miscellaneous materials. It's a slow and expensive process, but you may wish to check it out.

Obviously, Quartzite is Quartzite. Did you know that you could extract any excess Quartzite into §eLiquid Glass§r?

§aPotassium Feldspar§r electrolyses into some incredibly useful resources.

You also have a (low) chance for §dBiotite§r, which notably electrolyses for a very slow source of §bFluorine§r.

Finally, §aMetal Mixture dust§r is useless until you can centrifuge it at §5EV§r. Pretty much all of its outputs when centrifuged are very useful.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.q_52868f643f0a1:
Just Forge Hammer that Cobblestone and you'll get some §dGravel§r.

Gravel macerates into §6Stone Dust§r, but with a low chance of Flint when the recipe is performed in a §6HV Macerator§r or above. You probably want to sift for Flint, anyway!

Flint Dust centrifuges into §aSilicon Dioxide§r, which is then electrolysed for Silicon and Oxygen.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.q_10fd7c65fc83a: Two vast and trunkless legs of stone...

Yet another §bForge Hammer§r step, but you'll be making §dSand§r renewably. With renewable Sand comes renewable Glass (remember to try using an §9Arc Furnace§r for that sweet §adoubled§r yield!).

Quartz Sand Dust centrifuges into a chanced output of §3Certus Quartz§r Dust.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.q_471b85b964c57:
Yup - §brenewable§r Glass.

Glass'll always be useful throughout your playthrough in a variety of recipes.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.q_43d5a5f95eeb3:
Pulverise your Diorite into Dust, then centrifuge for Mirabilite Dust and Clay Dust.

Mirabilite yields minimal Sulfur, but Clay Dust is the real treasure here. When electrolysed, you'll get some Aluminium for your troubles. Not bad!
phoenix_chronicles.quest.q_0089aa3a92c02:
Granite Dust centrifuges into Redrock Dust and the familiar Silicon Dioxide Dust.

Silicon Dioxide is generally just great to have, and Redrock centrifuges into Calcite (that's renewable Calcium) and Flint.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.q_3b436487305ae:
Deepslate centrifuges into... you guessed it... Silicon Dioxide! You may want to set this up for the guaranteed Biotite output, as Biotite electrolyses into Fluorine.

This is obviously a far better source of Biotite than Stone Dust. Hopefully, you didn't waste your time setting that up!
phoenix_chronicles.quest.q_3bca8923df575:
Andesite Dust will get you some delicious Asbestos Dust, and some Saltpeter Dust to boot.

Asbestos is a slow source of Magnesium, and Saltpeter has a variety of uses in chemistry.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.q_71972471afb97:
By placing some Redstone Dust into your Rock Breaker, you'll find yourself making some Obsidian.

Obsidian Dust is quite useful, as it electrolyses into Iron.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.q_1937057c27596:
Basalt Dust centrifuges into Olivine, a material which can be used to substitute Emerald in a small handful of recipes - for example, when making Engraved Crystal Chips.

You also get a pittance of Dark Ash.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.q_789e2dc829dd1:
Not to be confused with regular Granite, Red Granite has some useful utility when the dust is processed.

Electrolysing it yields Aluminium for slightly fewer steps than the renewable Clay electrolysis.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.q_3e3eb69f34f50: Marble Dust isn't anything to write home about, yielding Calcite and Magnesium.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.all_kinds_of_ai: Things are up in the air right now...

By collecting Air with a §6Gas Collector§r and cooling it to Liquid state with a §3Vacuum Freezer§r, you can then distill the liquid Air for a plethora of valuable resources.

You thought that was all? Air collection isn't limited to the §2Overworld§r - whilst you'll require a higher-tier Distillation Tower to distill the "higher" tiers of liquid Air, you can also process air from the §4Nether§r and the §5End§r. This process is mostly optional, but you'll definitely find it to be a rewarding one.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.liquid_ender_ai: Nitrogen, Oxygen, Helium, Krypton, Xenon, Radon, Ender Pearls...

§5Ender Air§r is probably the most interesting of the three airs to distill. Requiring an §9IV Distillation Tower§r and distilling in batches of 200,000L, you'll need to outfit your DT with at least an §9IV§r Input Hatch (or an §5ME Hatch§r if you're inclined).

You're getting a ton of Nitrogen, Oxygen, Helium, and Deuterium - the latter of which is commonly used in §aFusion§r. Tritium is used to make §6Helium Plasma§r, which is commonly agreed to be the best plasma for §2power generation§r.

---


Krypton and Xenon are your run-of-the-mill §aEBF-boosting§r Noble gases. At this point, you should consider running most (if not all) of your EBF recipes on §bCircuit 2§r to benefit from the faster durations.

Would you look at that - you get §dRadon§r as well! It's a slow process, especially when you consider that your old setup (did you set it up?) already loops on itself, but §dmore Radon§r is nice.

Last but not least, you're getting a low chance of §3Ender Pearl Dust§r. The chances are low enough that you shouldn't give up on the Mixer recipe just yet... but once again, more §3Ender Pearls§r are nice!
phoenix_chronicles.task.liquid_ender_air: I'm surprised I can breathe in the End.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.liquid_air.desc:
This was touched upon in the §5EV§r chapter, but we'll focus on what this distillation gets you here.

The Nitrogen output is §bsubstantial§r, and can help you keep any §ePyrolyse Ovens§r running. You should buffer some of the Nitrogen so you can §aboost your EBFs§r - faster recipe times save your sanity and energy in equal measures.

---


Helium and Argon yields are low, but ideally you can run the Air Distillation as a §dpassive process§r every so often to keep your supplies topped up. Both are used to §aboost EBF speeds§r.

§bCrushed Ice§r is... well, §bCrushed Ice§r. Maybe you could open a cocktail bar?
phoenix_chronicles.task.liquid_air_task_: I promise I won't sell my air as a commodity!
phoenix_chronicles.quest.liquid_nether_a:
Carbon Monoxide is useful when making §6Butyraldehyde§r for your Laminated Glass in §9late IV§r.

§6Coal Gas§r can be processed in a Distillation Tower for a variety of useful outputs.

Helium-3 is only used in §bFusion§r, and Neon is used to boost a single §aBlast Furnace§r recipe - §4UHV§r superconductors!

Ashes are always useful for the handful of resources they grant.
phoenix_chronicles.task.liquid_nether_ai: It's not all hellish in the Nether.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.what_about_my_m: Is it safe? Is it alright?

Just so you're aware - vanilla farms such as §7Iron Golems§r or §ePiglins§r have been §4disabled§r in this pack. There are obviously ways to cheese the pack (such as some good old Minecraft §acapitalism§r, §mif you catch our drift§r), but we encourage you to try to play without taking advantage of some notorious vanilla "§ocheese§r".

It's possible that in the future, we'll just make a core-mod for the pack, so players can re-enable the disabled mob drops. For now, the drops are disabled via §5KubeJS script§r, so if you're script-savvy, the file can be removed at §o§7server_scripts/vanilla/loot_drops.js§r.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.pyrolyse_oven.d:
The §3Pyrolyse Oven§r is an electric equivalent to the §3Coke Oven§r. It can produce §9Coal Coke§r and §9Charcoal§r with a §9Creosote§r byproduct just as before, but also has additional §6Organic Byproducts§r, the most beneficial of these being §aWood Tar§r.

Another product is §aBiomass§r, which is more pertinent for your progression as of this moment.

---


The byproducts can be Distilled for an array of organic resources, with §odifferent§r byproducts giving §odifferent§r ratios of §odifferent§r chemicals.

You will need to take a peek at the §9Distillation§r Quest to get to grips with the power of distillation...

---


There are recipes that can accept §bNitrogen§r to double the speed. This isn't quite worth pursuing right now, but Nitrogen will eventually be free and infinite.

You should be more than fine with a single §3LV Energy Hatch§r, and Superconductors to supply a steady §d64 EU/t§r. Additionally, §3Cupronickel Coils§r are perfect when you're getting used to the Pyrolyse Oven, but you may want to upgrade to §bKanthal§r eventually.


---


§9§lNote:§r§l The Plant path is one path you can take towards §9§lEthylene§r§l, which is a necessary chemical in progressing to §6HV§r§l. The other path involves Oil.§r

The Pyrolyse Oven remains §doptional§r. However, it is very rewarding to construct one either for Power, or for the various Byproducts, and we highly recommend you give it a look.

§l§3Lore:§r§o In GT5u, the structure for the Pyrolyse Oven was infamously a giant box with only 9 coils inside. Players usually spent several minutes debugging what is wrong due to a lack of a EMI preview.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.biomass.title: Biomass
phoenix_chronicles.quest.biomass.descrip:
Welcome to the §2natural§r Ethylene route! This method uses §9plant matter§r to produce Ethanol.

Before we get ahead of ourselves, §aSugar Cane§r works fine in a §3Brewery§r for a decent yield of Biomass.

Othe§rrwise, you could try the "§o§dPlantball into Bio Chaff§r" route, and then turn it into Biomass, either in the §3Brewery§r or the §3Pyrolyse Oven§r - the latter being more efficient.

§9Note:§r Only one Bio Chaff can be obtained from maceration until you make the §3HV Macerator§r.

---


§l§3Lore:§r§o You may recognise Plantballs from IndustrialCraft2! In IC2 Experimental, there was this rather... obscure way to turn Biomass into Biogas for power, which sadly required too much investment to be really worth it.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.local_brewery_s:
The Brewery can be used to make §aLubricant§r from §aRedstone§r and §aCreosote§r/§aOil§r. Lubricant has some niche uses, namely being used in the §3Cutter§r to significantly reduce the duration of its recipes.

The Brewery is a very, very slow machine, but it requires almost no power to run its recipes. Building §2many Breweries§r will help you obtain enough Biomass on your quest for plastic. Oh, and you can use it to brew §dPotions§r too!

§9Note:§r The Brewery "unlocks" the Biomass path towards §9Ethylene§r. The same can be done in the §3Pyrolyse Oven§r. The other path involves Oil.§r

---


§l§3Lore:§r§o You could make your own Brewery if you want to build up a company and start selling Booze... in GregTech 6.§r
phoenix_chronicles.quest.ethylene.title: Ethylene
phoenix_chronicles.quest.ethylene.descri:
Our warmest congratulations on making it here.

The way you should obtain §aEthylene§r was described in the previous Quest, depending on the route you chose.

§aEthylene§r will shortly be used in polymer production. It's also useful in a few other reactions.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.ethanol.title: Ethanol
phoenix_chronicles.quest.ethanol.descrip:
Put your previously made §aBiomass§r into a §3MV Distillery§r to make §aEthanol§r.

You will need this for §dEthylene§r by reacting it with §aSulfuric Acid§r in a §3MV Chemical Reactor§r... unless you chose to go down the Oil path.

Once you have a hefty starting stock of Ethanol, consider making and distilling §9Fermented Biomass§r in a §3Distillation Tower§r (when you get there!) for extra chemicals.

§cDo not try§r to use Ethanol as a Power source... it's quite possibly its worst use. If it's organic §9Power§r that you want, we suggest taking a look at §dBenzene§r instead!
phoenix_chronicles.quest.naphtha.title: Naphtha
phoenix_chronicles.quest.naphtha.subtitl: We're still confused on how this is pronounced
phoenix_chronicles.quest.naphtha.descrip:
Distillating §aOil§r will give you Fuel that you will need to desulfurize.

§aHydrogen Sulfide§r is perfectly §drecycled§r in an §3Electrolyzer§r.

To automate this process, simply place your §3Chemical Reactor§r and your §3Electrolyzer§r next to each other. Be sure to use your §5Screwdriver§r to §4enable input from the output side§r.

§aNaphtha§r is a good §9Product§r source. Keep following the quests to the right for more details.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.fuel_cracking.s: Fuel and oil cracking can get complicated...
phoenix_chronicles.quest.fuel_cracking.d:
Don't panic! We'll mostly be doing this to get hydrocarbons.

There are many ways to acquire §dEthylene§r from Oil processing. It's easy to get lost in all the options and recipes!

The best way is to steam-crack §aNaphtha§r in a §3Chemical Reactor§r. Be sure to make the §aSeverely Steam-Cracked§r version for a higher yield of Ethylene.

---


Once in §6HV§r, you'll have the option to do this recipe in the §3Cracking Unit§r at 100% efficiency. Unfortunately, the recipes you are doing with the Chemical Reactor have a loss of §450%§r.

§9Note:§r All of this looks and feels terribly inefficient - we hope that's strong motivation to tier up! The §3Distillation Tower§r will be a huge upgrade for petrochem, but you're not quite there... yet. Right now, you'll have to use a §3Distillery§r to get §dEthylene§r.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.electricity_gen:
Higher-tier Generators will increase their fuel consumption proportionally to their Generation rate, keeping the duration of fuels and the specific amount of energy from fuels the same. The §3Advanced Steam Turbine§r will use §d5,120 mB Steam§r per second, equivalent to §d256 mB/t§r.

Get §eany§r of the generators to complete this quest, but you may prefer starting off with the §3Advanced Steam Turbine§r.

---


There are a few new power options available for §bMV§r. Selecting the Generators and pressing §4U§r will let you see which fuels count as §aCombustion§r or §aGas§r.

Quests in the top left corner of this Chapter are for the valuable Power options.

If you stick to §9Steam§r for your Power generation, you'll probably need a couple §3High Pressure Boilers§r.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.frost_reinforce:
Any Steel you encounter in day-to-day life is most likely §7Stainless Steel§r. It is extremely resilient against corrosion.§r We have, however, gone with §bReinforced Frost Stained Steel§r, a custom alloy made to withstand both high and cold temperatures.

Reinforced Frost Stained Steel is the material for §6HV§r components, like §bAluminfrost§r for §bMV§r and §6Aurum Steel§r for §7LV§r. Normal Stainless Steel is also used in high quantities for the §3Distillation Tower§r.

It requires §cChromium§r, obtained mainly from §cRuby§r, §2Manganese§r, obtained from §2Pyrolusite§r and others in its vein, §bFrost§r, obtained by extracting §3permafrost§r dust, and §8Carbon§r, obtained by electrolyzing either coal or charcoal dust.

---


Smelting Reinforced Frost Stained Steel requires §dHV Power§r, which you likely do not have at this point. Scaling Power Production is crucial.

If you §9haven't already§r, it would be a good idea to get a second EBF going. They can share blocks, so that means your second EBF only requires §a10 Cupronickel Coils§r instead of 16.

Have one EBF run off §bMV§r for Aluminium and any other recipes requiring §bMV§r Power, and one running off §6HV§r with §32 MV Energy Hatches§r.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.transformers.de:
§3Transformers§r allow you to step up and down safely between Voltage tiers. They convert the power they receive into an equivalent amount of power 1 voltage tier above or below the input voltage.

Apart from running machines on different voltage tiers, Transformers come in handy for transporting power across longer distances, as cable loss has less of an effect at higher voltages. Just like real life!

---


Transformers have 5 low voltage sides, and 1 high voltage side.

The §9normal§r Transformer can only do 1A <-> 4A conversion, but §9Adjustable§r Transformers can be changed between 1A <-> 4A, 2A <-> 8A, 4A <-> 16A, and 16A <-> 64A conversions.

Use a §aSoft Hammer§r to change between transforming up and down, and a §aScrewdriver§r on Adjustable Transformers to change the amperage.

Higher tier Transformers will require §9Coils§r.
If you're wanting to dive into §bMV§r, start here.

The dusts created in an §3MV Mixer§r have great utility.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.mv_components.s: Hated crafting these in the previous tier?
phoenix_chronicles.quest.mv_components.d:
Here's a list of the components you will need in §bMV§r. To alleviate the pain, be sure to autocraft or §dbulk-craft§r these parts, especially §aMotors§r.

Familiar with the §aEmitter§r? This tier's Emitter requires a §dFlawless Emerald§r in its recipe, which'll be only attainable with the §3Sifting Machine§r for now.

Conveyors, Pumps and Robot Arms are objective upgrades to §7LV§r versions if you use them as covers.

§6This quest unlocks a new tutorial on Overclocking in the §lTips and Tricks§r§6 tab - check it out to learn more!§r
phoenix_chronicles.quest.advanced_electr: We made it to MV, and, well...
The Advanced Electrolyzer allows you to decompose §6far more§r Dusts. This will make getting materials such as §aAluminium§r§o a lot§r easier!
phoenix_chronicles.quest.digital_miner.d:
This kind soul§r will mine ores for you when placed above a vein.

Vertical range is unlimited below the miner. Horizontal range is displayed in the tooltip.

The §bMV§r variant may not have the range to mine a full vein, but the §6HV§r variant does, so you may wish hold off for now. Get §eeither§r to complete this Quest.

---


You will need §9Power§r. §aCharged Batteries§r may work, but they tend to run out of power, which is a bit inconvenient.

Our top suggestion is to use a filled §3Drum§r of some kind of fuel §7(if you're using Steam, no dice!)§r and a §3Generator§r.

Place the Drum above your Generator and right-click it with a §5Screwdriver§r to auto-output into the Generator.

---


§cNote:§r Do not forget to §dchunkload§r all 9 chunks of the ore vein with FTB Utilities §7(open the map in the top left corner, claim the chunks with left-click, and enable force loading with shift-left-click)§r.

§9Tip:§r You can either use an §3ME Chest§r or a §32x2 Drawer§r as the output inventory to make transporting the ores back home a simple task. The §3ME Chest§r can be powered with EU directly.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.steel_alloys.de:
Vanadiumsteel is required in small quantities in progression. It's §6nearly four times as durable§r as Steel if used in GregTech tools. The Vanadium comes from §aVanadium Magnetite§r, which you may have encountered in Magnetite veins.

Other Steel alloys include Blue Steel, Red Steel, and Black Steel!

Take some Blue Steel free of charge - it's twice as durable as Steel.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.autocrafting.de:
§3Molecular Assemblers§r can be used to automate Crafting Table recipes, which means you can automate just about anything now.

To maximise the number of recipes a single Molecular Assembler can do, make a 3D matrix of Molecular Assemblers and ME Interfaces - where each component is surrounded on 6 sides by the other.

Using higher-tier materials in crafting will yield more Molecular Assemblers.

---


§cWarning:§r Try to avoid using GT tools in AE2 autocrafting! It causes AE2 to freak out... you may or may not destroy the TPS, or even worse, end up having thousands of tools being crafted as soon as one of them breaks.

If you're stubborn enough to §oreally§r want to use GT tools in AE2 autocrafting, prioritise encoding recipes that use tools with high durability, but §4do not§r setup autocrafting for the tools themselves. Instead, use the alternate §3Assembling Machine§r recipes.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.pressing_matter:
Making §aAE2 Presses§r will unlock all the §9Processors§r from AE2. This opens up §9ME Drives§r, §9ME Interfaces,§r §9ME Crafting CPUs§r... that's almost the rest of AE2 at your fingertips! §7(Or at least... not until you obtain Silicon Ingots.)§r

AE2 §9Printed Circuits§r are now made in the §3Forming Press§r.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.advanced_cutter:
The §3MV Cutter§r is required to cut §7Silicon Boules§r to prepare them for §aLaser Engraving§r.

We recommend you supply this machine with a steady stream of §dLubricant§r to cut down on the processing time.

Lubricant can be §3brewed§r from §eOil§r and §aTalc§r, §2Soapstone§r or §cRedstone§r.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.laser_engraving:
The §3Laser Engraver§r engraves patterns into §9Silicon Wafers§r based on the type of §9Lens§r it is given. After the wafers are engraved, they must be passed through a §3Cutting Machine§r to turn them into components ready to be put into Circuits.

Higher tier Engravers can etch more complex wafers for more efficient Circuits.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.upgrade_your_eb:
A §7LV§r Battery Buffer and two §7LV§r Energy Hatches likely won't cut it anymore. Let's remedy that!

Upgrade your Electric Blast Furnace with a §3MV Energy Hatch§r. Now, you can run it with §bMV§r Generators without having to mess around with §3Transformers§r.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.advanced_assemb:
The §3Assembler§r is a staple for every Tier; an important goal to unlock more recipes and progress further into the Age. Many in the community see crafting a voltage tier's Assembler as a sign of §oproperly§r reaching said voltage.

That being said, welcome to §bMV§r!

The §bMV §3Assembler§r unlocks §eTransistors§r, §eCapacitors§r and §eInductors§r, used for the next tiers of Circuits.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.kanthal_coils.s: Is it getting hot in here?
phoenix_chronicles.quest.kanthal_coils.d:
§3Kanthal Heating Coils§r are the next major step in progression. They increase the temperature of your §3Blast Furnace§r to §d2,700K§r, allowing you to process new materials. They may also §eaccelerate§r less hot recipes - check the quest to the top-left for details.

You will need a staggering §a128 Ingots§r for a full set of Coils, which will easily take over an hour. We advise that you move on to other projects while your §3EBF§r is hard at work - that or build another one!

---


An §3MV Chemical Bath§r is required to cool §cHot Ingots§r down. They're §chot§r when held, as the name implies. §o§7Maybe you should save your hands and automate this...§r

With the construction of a §3Kanthal EBF§r, you're now able to make §dSilicon Ingots§r, opening up the vast majority of AE2!
phoenix_chronicles.quest.250iq.title: 250IQ
phoenix_chronicles.quest.250iq.subtitle: Stop burning your darn hands!
phoenix_chronicles.quest.250iq.descripti:
This is a guide on how to automatically route §lall§r your Hot Ingots to your Chemical Bath, while keeping everything automated in tip-top shape.

The cheap way would be to use filters, and manually add Hot Ingots one by one... which is so boring! Let's try the fun option.

Install an §aItem Tag Filter§r Cover on the side of your §3Chemical Bath§r, open it and set it to whitelist "§e§lhot_ingots§r".

From here, you can route with §9any logistics system§r of your choice.

---


Connect the output of your §3EBF(s)§r to the input of your §3Chemical Bath§r and the output dump (Chest or Crate).
You can also have a §dRestrictive Pipe§r in front of the output dump to ensure the Chemical Bath will be prioritized.

§l§9Note:§r If you wish to know more tags for more automation setups, they will display if you press Shift when hovering over an item. For instance, an item tagged with §e§o#forge:plates/copper§r would be filtered as §e§lplates/copper§r.

§9Other Note:§r The Item Tag Filter partially supports §dregex§r. Hover over the info icon for more information.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.moores_law.desc: A circuit component that you can now produce thanks to the §3MV Assembler§r and your shiny new §3Kanthal EBF§r.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.first_hv_circui: ...but hold on before getting too giddy

Alright... technically, obtaining §6HV§r Circuits and Stainless Steel lets you progress to §6HV§r - but let's not rush things.

The first thing you should make with these is a §3MV Circuit Assembler§r to unlock the new tier of Circuits right away; cheaper recipes is the §dreal payoff§r here.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.download_more_r: §aRandom Access Memory§r is required for more advanced Electronic Components.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.more_lv_circuit: You have unlocked a new tier of Circuits!
