The Integrated Logic Circuit is an alternate §7LV §aCircuit§r, which is easier to mass-produce, and can be upgraded to §bMV§r (and then §6HV§r).

§9Note:§r This is not a strict upgrade to the cost of Circuits - you would need to get to the next Tier for that, just slightly further down in §bMV§r. It is still an important upgrade, and is required to get to §6HV circuits§r.

---


§l§3Lore:§r§o The circuit progression in GTCEu is mostly based on GT5u's progression. It has been rebalanced to not be as painful. §lSpecifically§r§o this circuit tier, which was a trap!
phoenix_chronicles.quest.more_mv_circuit: The §bMV§r Circuit for the Integrated Tier.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.silicon_lottery:
§9Silicon Boules§r are made in the §3EBF§r with half a stack of §aSilicon Dust§r and a pinch of §aGallium Arsenide§r. Their primary purpose is engraving §6Circuit Wafers§r.

After making the Boule, process it in the §3Cutter§r to get 16 Silicon Wafers ready for engraving.

The recommended §aSilicon§r source at this point would be... hm, either §dGlass Dust§r or §dSodalite§r.

§cWarning:§r Each Silicon Boule takes §47.5 minutes§r to make at 120 EU/t, or 1,080,000 EU! If the EBF loses power midway, the recipe will start to §close progress§r.

With that being said, Silicon Boules take an absolute age to craft, so consider parallelizing the recipe in multiple §3EBF§rs and stockpiling them.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.advanced_circui:
As is common for every tier, the §3Circuit Assembler§r is an essential part of progression, always opening up a new Tier of circuits.

At this point you should be placing an §3Extractor§r next to your Circuit Assembler. Send off dozens of stacks of §aSoldering Alloy§r Ingots, and you won't have to worry about refilling again.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.ultimate_smelte: Possibly the most powerful furnace you've seen

At its lowest power (Cupronickel coils and §7LV§r Voltage), the §dMulti Smelter§r smelts 32 items in just 12 seconds - equivalent to §926.7 Furnaces§r, or 3.3 Steam Ovens!

If that wasn't already enough to convince you, standard §aoverclocks§r can be applied with sufficient voltage.

And even better - higher tier §3Coils§r increase the amount of items it can smelt in §dparallel§r!
phoenix_chronicles.quest.best_lv_circuit: It Feels Good to be the Best

§6The best LV Circuits§r! You can start to churn these guys out, as you'll be making them for the rest of the game.

Try to keep a stockpile of these crafted at all times - making these on-demand can take a while.

Reaching §5EV§r will unlock methods to make them even cheaper.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.best_mv_circuit:
§6The best MV Circuits§r! You will be making these for the remainder of the game.

Eventually (in §9IV§r), they will become even cheaper.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.first_ev_circui:
Your first §5EV§r Circuit gets a unique texture. If you still consider yourself to be in §bMV§r, §ahold off§r on making too many of these, as they won't benefit you right now. We can't stop you from making these if you §djust wanna flex§r on us, though.

It'll be needed in §6HV§r.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.more_hv_circuit:
Better §6HV§r Circuits - much §dcheaper§r and easier to make than before.

You should now be §aready to move on§r to the HV Chapter, unless you're yet to scale up your Power Production.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.capacitors.desc:
A circuit component that you can now produce thanks to the §3MV Assembler§r!

Capacitors are commonly used in computers to store information during power failures, amongst many other uses.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.blue_alloy.subt: You're blue now... that's my alloy
phoenix_chronicles.quest.blue_alloy.desc:
§aBlue Alloy§r is an excellent Cable material for §6HV§r power.

Nothing is preventing you from using it for §bMV§r power too! Make sure that you don't overvolt your machines, though.

Superconductors for both §bMV§r and §6HV§r are unlocked... later.

§aElectrotine§r is obtained from the §cNether§r, so don't craft it in the Mixer!

Furthermore, §aElectrotine§r can be separated for §dElectrum§r and §dRedstone§r.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.inductors.title: Inductors
phoenix_chronicles.quest.inductors.descr:
A Circuit Component that you can now make thanks to the §3MV Assembler§r.

If you want the cheapest recipe, §aNickel-Zinc Ferrite§r is the way to go.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.polyethylene.de:
If you want to be less fancy, just call it plastic.

For the polymerization process, add §aOxygen§r, which gives better returns than Air, then solidify like you would with Rubber.

§aPolyethylene (PE)§r is the key to unlocking §6many new things§r. It's commonly used as §dSheets§r, or in §dFluid§r form.

§l§3Lore:§r§o The OreDict and fluid name for Polyethylene in 1.12.2 GTCEu was §bplastic§f, for cross-mod compatibility.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.patterns.title: Patterns
phoenix_chronicles.quest.patterns.descri:
§aPatterns§r are used for AE2 autocrafting. Using §aPolyvinyl Chloride§r increases the yield by §64 times§r, and higher-tier plastics have even greater yields.

§3Molecular Assemblers§r aren't available for a little while more, but you can still automate machines with §9ME Interfaces§r.

A sub-note for autocrafting... whilst it's possible to perform chemical chains on-demand with AE2, doing so can build some bad habits that'll come back around to bite you in higher tiers. We urge you to passive things wherever you can.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.super_tank.desc:
No, but seriously.

This is the §cu§6l§et§ai§bm§9a§5t§4e§r portable Fluid storage solution. §64,000 buckets of storage§r - in one single block!

Like Drums, Super Tanks §6keep their fluids when broken§r, and can be cleared in the crafting grid.

If you hunger for §9even more§r storage, take a look at higher tier Super Tanks or AE2 Fluid Storage Cells.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.polyvinyl_chlor: You've already made one polymer, what's two?

§aPolyvinyl Chloride (PVC)§r is the 3rd-most produced plastic in real life. Here in CEu, it can be substituted for Polyethylene in the production of §aPlastic Circuit Boards§r and other items to increase the yield. It is required from §5EV§r onwards to wrap Cables.

PVC item pipes also have the §6highest throughput§r available for a while, but most of your setups right now won't need such speed. Still, it's good to keep this knowledge in your pocket.

§9Pro tip:§r The fluid form of PVC is never used in base GTCEu, so feel free to solidify all of it into sheets.
It's a Casio on a Plastic Board

At this point, you have all the tools available to start making Plastic Boards. Higher-tier polymers in future will increase your PCB yields substantially.

The recipe chains are starting to get pretty long, so we recommend processing large batches in two dedicated §3Chemical Reactors§r.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.sodium_persulfa: Let's etch some Copper off Circuit Boards!

§aSodium Persulfate§r can be used in §9Ore Processing§r in the §3Chemical Bath§r to get various bonus outputs you would not normally obtain. It's completely optional, but pretty rewarding.

§lWait, stop! That's only a distraction§r - the real topic of this Quest is...

§aSodium Persulfate§r and §aIron III Chloride§r are used to make cheaper §9Good Circuit Boards§r, as their inclusion cuts Silver usage by a factor of four.

They're also §drequired§r to make §9Plastic Circuit Boards§r.

---


Making §aSodium Persulfate§r will yield §aHydrochloric Acid§r as a coproduct, which you may re-use to make §aIron III Chloride§r. This should the best approach right now, but the decision is entirely yours.

With more automation later in the game, Iron III Chloride will be the cheaper and more straight forward path.

This Quest requires §eboth§r Fluids to complete. You'll need both anyway...
phoenix_chronicles.quest.sulfuric_acid.s: "...what he thought was H2O was H2SO4!"
phoenix_chronicles.quest.sulfuric_acid.d:
EMI might look a little overwhelming here, so we'll go through the best path for Sulfuric Acid here.

Making §eSulfuric Acid§r is a three step process. It is used in many important reactions, so you should automate its production ASAP.

---


To automate it, you will need §3three LV Chemical Reactors§r. We would recommend building a dedicated setup somewhere with §3a single LV Generator§r to power all three machines. You can then spaghetti your pipes to handle input and output §m...or simply use AE2§r.

§9-§r Step 1: React §aSulfur§r with §bOxygen§r to form §aSulfur Dioxide§r.
§9-§r Step 2: React §aSulfur Dioxide§r with more §bOxygen§r to form §aSulfur Trioxide§r.
§9-§r Step 3: React §aSulfur Trioxide§r with §bWater§r to form §eSulfuric Acid§r.

---


§l§3Lore:§r§o GregTech 5's Chemical Reactor only had one Fluid slot. To circumvent that, they would do §dcell chemistry§f. The way you would automate Sulfuric Acid was by having one cell travel from machine to machine and then loop back to its starting position. A somewhat fun and interesting automation challenge, but also a chore!
phoenix_chronicles.quest.hydrochloric_ac: You'll need a lot of this!

Obtain §9Hydrochloric Acid§r by mixing §aHydrogen§r and §aChlorine§r.

This acid is also obtained as waste from a lot of reactions involving §aChlorine§r. Depending on your setups, you may never need to produce it directly.

---


§cNote:§r We have a $medicine command on our Discord:

"§b§oDo not attempt this in real life - it is not only illegal, but also stupidly dangerous§r".

This applies to toying with chemicals. Please don't do it.

Side note - we can guarantee you have a sample of this with you right now! It's in your stomach as a part of gastric acid.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.it_will_melt_yo:
You may notice that some fluids say they are "§aAcidic§r", with §9Sulfuric Acid§r being one of them.

This means that many fluid pipes will not be able to transport them safely!

At §bMV§r, the cheapest pipes for acid transportation are probably §aGold§r, with the more expensive §aVanadium Steel§r or §aChrome§r pipes taking second and third place.

§aStainless Steel§r or §aPolytetrafluoroethylene§r (try saying that fast) will be valid options once you are in §6HV§r.

---


You have three options for acid storage at around this point: §dGlass Vials§r, §dGold Drums§r, or §dSuper Tanks§r. Glass Vials are like §9Fluid Cells§r, and are made to store acids. Gold Drums are self-explanatory. Super Tanks will be unlocked after §9Polyethylene§r, and can store any fluid without restriction.

§cWARNING:§r Acids in the wrong pipes will cause §cvoiding§r, §cpipe burning§r, and high chance of §cdeath§r! Be careful!

§l§3Lore:§r§o The acid transportation and storage mechanics originate from GregTech 6.
phoenix_chronicles.task.it_will_melt_you: I'm an acid professional, don't worry
phoenix_chronicles.quest.better_batterie:
§bMV§r Batteries will appeal to you if you want to buffer Energy, just like §7LV§r.

The cost in §aSodium§r, §aLithium§r or §aCadmium§r jumps up to 8 dusts, so you should use whatever you have the most of. The difference in capacity isn't §7THAT§r huge, after all!

Get §eeither§r Battery to complete the Quest.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.advanced_extrud:
We §lSINCERELY§r hope at §cno§r point you made the §7LV§r Extruder, because only the §bMV§r Extruder is actually useful. If you did, immediately §arecycle it§r through the Arc Furnace.

The Extruder shapes solid materials into (almost!) any form using §aIngots§r. This is a great way to reduce the amount of microcrafting, as well as keeping a high conversion ratio.

The Extruder can make §6Bolts§r, §6§6Small Gears§r, §6Gears§r, and §6§6Rings§r at the highest efficiency in a single step!

You may also like to use it for §dPipes§r, §dLong Rods§r, and §dRotors§r.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.fluid_drilling_:
It's quite the investment to own a §3Fluid Drilling Rig§r, but it is §oby far§r the most prominent §6source of Oil§r.

It pumps fluids from underneath Bedrock itself. Note that the fluids aren't actually there, instead being simulated.

Fluid veins are stored within §cchunk-sized regions§r. Each vein has a different fluid, but they are mostly types of Oil. To check what the veins hold, shift right click your prospector to turn it on to fluid veins mode.


---


Each vein generates with a different base yield. This is typically between §d150L§r to §d300L per second§r.

When drained, fluid veins will slowly deplete. This will cause the fluid yield to decrease over time until it reaches its depletion yield. At that point, you should move the Rig to a different vein.

A §3Basic Fluid Drilling Rig§r will last for 100,000 operations (with 1 second per operation) until depletion. This is enough for §6well over 10,000§r buckets of Oil. Higher tier Rigs will massively increase the yield, while also decreasing the depletion rate.

---


§lWhat you can find in the §2Overworld§r§l:§r

§9Oil:§r richer in §aLight Fuel§r, the most appreciated variant.
§9Light Oil:§r richer in §aRefinery Gas§r, usable for power.
§9Heavy Oil:§r richer in §aHeavy Fuel§r, which has uses that are more niche.
§9Raw Oil:§r richer in §aNaphtha§r, the best source of the early-game oil products.
§9Natural Gas:§r grants §aRefinery Gas§r with no distillation required.
§l§9Salt Water:§r grants §aSodium§r and §aChlorine§r, useful later.

---


§lWhat you can find in the §cNether§r§l:§r

§9Natural Gas:§r grants §aRefinery Gas§r but with higher yield than the Overworld vein.
§9Lava:§r hopefully, you know what this is.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.us_simulator.su: Ever mined into an Oil deposit?
phoenix_chronicles.quest.us_simulator.de:
Get any kind of §3Pump§r, place it above an Oil spout and... give it some power.

Do §cnot§r pump above an Ocean, as the pump will attempt to pull water, resulting in getting the pump stuck. Sorry!

---


Each Oil deposit can have between §63,000§r and §69,200§r buckets of Oil, which is a LOT! Refining the Oil§r onsite into either §aLight Fuel§r or §aDiesel§r (or both) is perfectly viable. The next few Quests will explain each type's pros and cons.

Store any obtained Oil in §3Drums§r, but you would do yourself a favour to use a §3Super Tank§r as soon as you can make them.

§cWarning: §rDo not forget to §dchunkload§r with FTB Utilities (open the map in the top left corner, claim the chunks with left-click, and enable force loading with shift-left-click).

---


§9§lNote:§r§l The Oil path is one path towards §9§lEthylene§r§l. The other paths involve getting natural with some Ethanol.§r

For now, Oil is §doptional§r. It becomes mandatory much later when you get to §5EV§r.

Oil can also be refined in the form of §aLight Fuel§r, §aDiesel§r or even §aGasoline§r, which are excellent power options.

If you chose this path, you should use it for both Power and Ethylene.

Oil spouts are a §6great starting point§r - they will tide you over until you unlock Fluid Drilling Rigs.

---


§l§3Lore:§r§o Oil geysers were originally from Buildcraft. If you played a GregTech 5 modpack §cwithout§f Buildcraft, you needed to use the Fluid Rig and tap randomly to try and get lucky, or wait until §6HV§f, where prospecting for fluids was available.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.america_simulat: This quest was sponsored by the US Military

Underground, you may come across pure Oilsands ore veins. You can §3centrifuge§r the Dust to get §aOil§r.

§9§lNote:§r§l The Oil path is one path towards §9§lEthylene§r§l. The other paths involve getting natural with some Ethanol.§r

For now, Oil is §doptional§r. It becomes mandatory much later when you get to §5EV§r.

Oil can also be refined in the form of §aLight Fuel§r, §aDiesel§r or even §aGasoline§r, which are excellent power options.

If you chose this path, you should use it for both Power and Ethylene.

Oilsands are a §6great starting point§r - they'll tide you over until you unlock Fluid Drilling Rigs.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.distillery.desc:
Before we start, here's some important information if you're aiming to make Ethylene:

Taking the §aOil§r route will require §oat least§r a §3LV Distillery§r.

With the §aBiomass§r route, you will §lneed§r a §3MV Distillery§r.

Get §eeither§r to complete this quest.

---


Got all that? §6Alright§r! Let's discuss a complex topic: §9Distillation§r. We'll try to help you understand how and why the §aEMI§r recipes are the way they are, so stick with us.

Nearly all the §3Distillery§r recipes are duplicates from the §3Distillation Tower§r, except that they only have one Fluid output, and void everything else.

In other words, you could argue the §3Distillery§r is an §dinferior§r §3Distillation Tower§r.

---


This doesn't mean that the §3Distillery§r is the worse of the two. It is unlocked earlier, and it is §dsmaller§r, §dcheaper§r, and §dmore energy efficient§r per recipe.

Hell, in many cases, you won't even mind losing the other Fluids.

§3Distilleries§r are an essential component for power generation, whether you pick §aDiesel§r or §aBenzene§r.

You'll probably want many of them at as low-tier as possible to avoid the energy losses from Overclocking.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.the_church_of_n:
§aRefinery Gas§r, §aLPG§r and §aMethane§r are §9Gas Fuels§r. LPG (Liquid Petroleum Gas) is a mix of hydrocarbons typically used in heating appliances.

Refinery Gas is obtained either through §dNatural Gas§r or §dLight Oil§r, the latter yielding more, yet requiring an extra step of distillation.

Use of a §3Centrifuge§r to separate into §aLPG§r and §aMethane§r should always be done, as it's practically free.

---


§a§aLPG§r and §aMethane§r are burned in a §3Gas Turbine§r. Among the other fuel options, they are the easier to set up which makes them excellent to get started. Their drawback is that they cannot be refined further, so upgrading the §3Fluid Drilling Rig§r may be a top priority if you stick to this fuel source.

§aMethane§r can also be obtained from a few §anatural sources§r. §eBetween us§r, they're memes, but you can explore them if you wish. Ultimately, your power source is your choice.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.the_church_of_b: In the end, it's always Benzene

§aBenzene§r is a §9Gas Fuel§r. To skip some frustration, let's check out the two best ways to obtain it.

The first option is typically §dWood based§r. Put Logs in the §3Pyrolyse Oven§r for §9Wood Tar§r. The Charcoal you obtain can then be processed in §3Extractors§r for even more §9Wood Tar§r, which you §3distill§r for §aBenzene§r.

Your second option is §dHeavy Oil based§r. Put Heavy Oil in a §3Distillery§r for §9Heavy Fuel§r, which you §aseverely steam-crack§r and §3distill§r again for §aBenzene§r.

---


For information on how to process Oil, check the Light Fuel and Naphtha Quests.

In general, it is better to prioritize placing down more machines (§dparallelisation§r) over overclocking the recipes. That way, you end up losing less energy processing the resources.

§aBenzene§r is burned in a §3Gas Turbine§r. This power source starts weaker than its §eDiesel§r cousin, but gets a big boost when refined to §6Nitrobenzene§r in §6HV§r. Ultimately, your power source is your choice.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.light_fuel.subt: Turn up the Lights in here, baby
phoenix_chronicles.quest.light_fuel.desc:
Distillating §aOil§r will give you Fuel that you will need to desulfurize.

§aHydrogen Sulfide§r is perfectly §drecycled§r in an §3Electrolyzer§r.

To automate this process, simply place your §3Chemical Reactor§r and your §3Electrolyzer§r next to each other. Be sure to use your §5Screwdriver§r to §4enable input from the output side§r.

§aLight Fuel§r is a good §9Power§r option, but there's something even greater... check the Quest to the left.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.the_church_of_d:
§aDiesel§r is a §dOil-based §9Combustion Fuel§r.

To mix §aLight Fuel§r and §aHeavy Fuel§r, the right ratio for §3Distilleries§r is §63:2§r from §dOil§r or §dRaw Oil§r.

This would necessitate 3 Distilleries for Light Fuel, or 2 Distilleries for Heavy Fuel.

---


You can cut the amount of §dOil§r required §6drastically§r by using §dHeavy Oil§r for §aHeavy Fuel§r specifically. §dOilsands§r is a great option if you wish to go down this route!

§o(For the math nerds, you go from 8.33 Oil -> 6 Diesel, to 5 Oil + 0.4 Heavy Oil -> 6 Diesel)§r

§eNote:§r Do §cnot attempt§r to put Oil in the §3Distillation Tower§r You might think it's a good idea because it gives both Light Fuel and Heavy Fuel. However, this process requires a lot of overclocking to be worth your time, and you will lose more energy than what the byproducts are worth.

---


In general, it is better to prioritize placing down more machines (§dparallelisation§r) over overclocking the recipes. That way, you end up losing less energy processing the resources.

§aDiesel§r is burned in a §3Combustion Generator§r. It can be further refined to §6Cetane-Boosted Diesel§r in §6HV§r. Compared to the other power sources, it is generally more efficient, but a more demanding processing line. If you take the §eOil§r route for §aPolyethylene§r, this can work great with existing infrastructure. Ultimately, the power source you want to use is your choice.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.multiple_channe:
Regular §o§dGregTech§r Fluid Pipes can only transport one fluid type at a time.

§3Quadruple Fluid Pipes§r can transfer four different types of fluids. §3Nonuple Fluid Pipes§r can transfer nine different types! Useful for compact setups.

§3Nonuple Fluid Pipes§r will be useful in §5EV§r for handling the many outputs of the §3Distillation Tower§r.

Get §eeither§r to finish this quest.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.ic_chips.title: IC Chips
phoenix_chronicles.quest.ic_chips.descri:
Using a Ruby Lens, engrave a Silicon Wafer into an ILC Wafer.

This can be processed in a Cutter for IC Chips, which are important components that will be precious when improving upon your circuit crafting capabilities.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.ulpic_chips.des:
Using a Sapphire Lens, engrave a Silicon Wafer into an ULPIC Wafer.

This can be processed in a Cutter for ULPIC Chips, which are important for some multiblock components!
phoenix_chronicles.quest.longdistance_it: Wondering how to move those ores around?

§3Long-Distance Item Pipes§r can be used to send items across great distances. Place one endpoint at each end, and connect them with pipeline blocks.

These pipes instantly transfer from the input side to the output side.

They also have a minimum distance between pipe endpoints, so you can't use these for short-range operations.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.longdistance_fl: Wondering how to move that oil around?

§3Long-Distance Fluid Pipes§r can be used to send fluids across great distances. Place one endpoint at each end, and connect them with pipeline blocks.

These pipes instantly transfer from the input side to the output side.

They also have a minimum distance between pipe endpoints, so you can't use these for short-range operations.

---


These pipes have a reputation of being §4buggy§r to set up. If they don't seem to work at first, try rotating the endpoints with a §eWrench§r.
Tired of running around your base yet? §3Travel Anchors§r make their introduction in the latest update!

Aim the §aTravel Staff§r at a placed Anchor, then §6sneak-right-click§r to teleport on top. You can §bcustomise the appearance§r of a Travel Anchor by right-clicking it with a block in your off-hand, and you can §9rename§r Anchors in their GUI. The effective tool for breaking them is the §bWrench§r.

The §dEnder Pearls§r necessary to craft more Anchors won't be available yet - take a small handful of Anchors to make life a §olittle§r easier.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.i_believe_i_can:
This Jetpack takes most §aCombustion Fuels§r (excluding oils) to enable a primitive form of flight.

Fill it like you would fill a Drum, or with a §3Canning Machine§r.

Press §4H§r (default) to enable Hover Mode.
I Believe I Can Fly II

This jetpack enables flight, and requires energy.

Charge it like you would charge a Battery.

Press §4H§r (default) to enable Hover Mode.

§o§8(Yeah, yeah, a jetpack is supposed to work off "propellants". Y'all are always here to nitpick.)§r
phoenix_chronicles.quest.tricorder.title: Tricorder
phoenix_chronicles.quest.tricorder.descr:
The §aPortable Scanner§r, or §aTricorder§r, is GTCEu's debug tool.

Using it will show you a block's details, the details of the energy network, its current status and contents, and its impact on performance.

It'll also display a percentage of fluid remaining in the fluid vein for the §3Fluid Rigs§r.

---


§l§3Lore:§r§o This little useful device comes from GregTech 5. It was extremely useful in the early days, because very little information (basically nothing) was given by GUIs or WAILA.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.200iq.title: 200IQ
phoenix_chronicles.quest.200iq.subtitle: Knock, knock - who's that? It's MENSA!
phoenix_chronicles.quest.200iq.descripti:
In this quest, we'll bestow upon you §5cursed wisdom§r... the ability to easily automate the Electrolyzer.

The §9Smart Item Filter§r is a filter that recognises Recipe Maps. When placed on the side of a machine, you can set it to "§3Electrolyzer§r" to allow insertion of electrolyzable items specifically. You heard that right - no need to filter manually!

Oh, and it only gets §abetter§r. If you combine this bad boy with a §aRobot Arm§r, it'll only supply the §6exact amount§r of items required for a successful recipe to the machine.

---


Place the §aRobot Arm§r on your Electrolyzer, open its GUI, then place the §9Smart Filter§r inside. Ensure that the Smart Filter is set to Electrolyzer.

Next, configure it to §d§lImport§r and §d§lSupply Exact§r. Finally, attach any inventory §7(a chest will do)§r onto the side where you placed the §aRobot Arm§r. Ta-dah! You've figured out how to handle §6all§r Electrolyzer recipes!

What about the output of the §3Electrolyzer§r? You may want to route the Fluids to several Tanks - or even §3Super Tanks§r if you've gotten that far. We highly recommend that you avoid any methods involving voiding Fluids.§7.§8. except for Water for obvious reasons.

---


§9Note:§r The Robot Arm has to facilitate the item transfer for its filtering functionality to work! Inserting directly into the machine §7(for instance, pushing with a Hopper!)§r will ignore the Robot Arm's §dSupply Exact§r setting.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.q_0db46141978be: Now that you have some §bAluminium,§r these are a further upgrade to your chests and backpacks. Unlocks another upgrade slot as a bonus.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.q_76e52a2c71962: Increases the storage space of your §bfluid§r and §8item§r drawers by 4 times!
phoenix_chronicles.quest.mv_superconduct: §a4A§r of §bMV§r energy transmission may be appealing, but you probably don't need these at this point. The option is always there if you need it.
You'll be an expert by the time you finish reading this!

Some of the details are repeated from the introduction quest, but we feel like we needed to expand on the explanation if you want to know all the details!

Ready for some "light" reading?

---


Each vein can contain up to four different ores.

Ore veins generate in a §4Grid§r. Every vein is spaced by 3 chunks from one to another in a cardinal direction.

They spawn at the §4Center§r of the Chunks which have both their X and Z coordinates be at §b1 plus a multiple of 3§r (-8, -5, -2, 1, 4, 7, ...). You will typically find two veins in the selected chunk - one will be in the Stone layer, and the other vein lays deeper in the Deepslate layer.

However, Ore veins may be deleted by caves, Oil deposits, or from trying to generate above the ground.

---


It's a good practice to make §dWaypoints§r to every vein you find, and to label their type. You may want to come back to it several times.

A typical Ore vein is §d7 blocks§r tall, and ores generate in 4 different patterns:
- The §9Top Ore§r generates in the higher 4 layers of the vein.
- The §9Bottom Ore§r generates in the lower 3 layers of the vein.
- The §9Between Ore§r generates in the middle 3 layers of the vein.
- The §9Sporadic Ore§r generates anywhere in the vein. There will be the least amount of this ore in a vein.

The same ore type can be in 2 different generation patterns, such as in Cassiterite veins.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.limonite.title: Limonite
phoenix_chronicles.quest.limonite.descri: A standard Iron vein. It's a good target when you need to replenish your supply.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.magnetite.title: Magnetite
phoenix_chronicles.quest.magnetite.descr:
This vein is namely one of the few direct sources of Gold in the overworld.

There are many other sources of Gold in GregTech, but you will likely see better yields of Gold if you obtain it by processing other resources.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.pyrite.title: Pyrite
phoenix_chronicles.quest.pyrite.subtitle: Source of Copper, Iron
phoenix_chronicles.quest.pyrite.descript:
An excellent Iron-Copper hybrid vein.

Chalcopyrite will play an integral role in the late game, when you're looking to get your hands on some Platinum Group Sludge.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.chalcopyrite.de:
A great vein for the early game. Copper and Tin to make Bronze, Realgar for your first source of Arsenic, and Zeolite for... nothing much.

---


§l§3Lore:§r§o As GregTech used to auto-generate its recipes, Zeolite used to electrolyze in batches of 141 dust at a time. Whoops!
phoenix_chronicles.quest.cassiterite.des: A pure, very rich Tin vein - excellent for early game. You'll be over the moon to find one of these in the §6Steam Age§r.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.cassiterite_san:
A decent alternative to the pure Tin vein if you haven't found one yet.

The other ores are as good as decoration.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.coal.title: Coal
phoenix_chronicles.quest.coal.subtitle: Source of pollution
phoenix_chronicles.quest.coal.descriptio:
As an ore, Coal is hardly worth large-scale processing, because there are too many additional steps. required to turn it into usable fuel. It's still good to have some in your back pocket.

Just run it through a Furnace.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.graphite.title: Graphite
phoenix_chronicles.quest.graphite.descri:
Your only source of Diamond!

Diamond has §6five times more durability§r than Iron for tools. The catch is that you'll need Diamond Plates for some tools, which is gated behind the Cutting Machine.

Diamond and Graphite both electrolyze into a ton of Carbon. Hint, hint..?

§cNote:§r Avoid macerating Diamonds in the early game. Recovering gem dusts into the actual gem cannot be done for a while - and even then, the process is slow and time-consuming...
phoenix_chronicles.quest.gamer_rage.subt: Source of Salt, Chlorine, Lithium, Fluorine
phoenix_chronicles.quest.gamer_rage.desc:
Your one-stop-shop for sources of Chlorine.

If you're pining after Lithium, note that it can be obtained from Lepidolite Ore Processing.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.olivine.title: Olivine
phoenix_chronicles.quest.olivine.descrip:
This vein starts to become notable for its Magnesium output starting in the midgame.

Olivine also has various uses, as it can substitute §aEmerald§r in a couple of recipes.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.garnet.title: Garnet
phoenix_chronicles.quest.garnet.subtitle: Source of Necklaces
phoenix_chronicles.quest.garnet.descript:
It's shiny! That's about it!

Yeah, you wish you could make jewelry out of it.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.apatite.title: Apatite
phoenix_chronicles.quest.apatite.descrip:
Hey, anyone remember Forestry?

This is pretty much the one vein you want to tap in for Phosphorus - which requires quite a few steps of processing to obtain.

Pyrochlore will eventually become extremely valuable, as it's a good source of Niobium.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.redstone.title: Redstone
phoenix_chronicles.quest.redstone.subtit: Source of Redstone, Ruby, Chromium, Mercury
phoenix_chronicles.quest.redstone.descri:
Your classic Redstone vein.

Ruby is very important for the Chromium it contains. You'll quickly discover that you can never have too much Chromium!
phoenix_chronicles.quest.sapphire_6efe.d:
Both Sapphire variants serve as your primary source of Aluminium until you can unlock other electrolysis recipes in §bMV§r.

The other two gems are mediocre at best.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.oilsands.title: Oilsands
phoenix_chronicles.quest.oilsands.descri:
A good source of §6Heavy Oil§r, which is useful for §6Diesel§r setups early on.

If you don't want to spend time processing Oilsands through your setup, you can always just §bCentrifuge§r it directly to get the Heavy Oil.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.soapstone.title: Soapstone
phoenix_chronicles.quest.soapstone.descr:
This one's nothing but a meme. It's literally called a Lubricant vein.

With that being said, Lubricant is always useful for your §eCutting Machines§r to keep your factory running smoothly.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.lapis.title: Lapis
phoenix_chronicles.quest.lapis.subtitle: Source of Lapis Lazuli, Aluminium, Sodium, Chlorine
phoenix_chronicles.quest.lapis.descripti:
Did you know Lazurite and Sodalite can be used as substitutes for §9Lapis§r in enchanting?

Sodalite is the most valuable Ore here, thanks to its useful electrolysis recipe when you get to §bMV§r.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.pyrolusite.desc:
Pyrolusite is what most people are here for. It smelts directly into Manganese, which you'll be needing in bulk for §6HV§r.

Tantalite will eventually become extremely valuable, thanks to its Niobium byproducts, and its utility when crafting §bSMD Components§r.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.galena.title: Galena
phoenix_chronicles.quest.galena.subtitle: Source of Lead, Silver
phoenix_chronicles.quest.galena.descript: The most consistent source of Lead and Silver.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.nickel.title: Nickel
phoenix_chronicles.quest.nickel.subtitle: Source of Nickel, Cobalt
phoenix_chronicles.quest.nickel.descript: Your one and only trusty source for Nickel.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.mica.title: Mica
phoenix_chronicles.quest.mica.subtitle: Source of Aluminium, Fluorine, Titanium
phoenix_chronicles.quest.mica.descriptio:
A source of Bauxite for your first ever Titanium.

Kyanite and Mica decompose into some desirable products if you electrolyze them, but there are definitely better options, so you shouldn't hunt them down if you want their byproducts.

§8(This vein probably irks your average GTNH player...)§r
phoenix_chronicles.quest.mineral_sand.de:
The worst Iron vein. It's helpful in the early game, but that's about it.

We love you anyway, Mineral Sand vein!
phoenix_chronicles.quest.bastnatite.subt: Source of Rare Earth, Neodymium, Fluorine
phoenix_chronicles.quest.bastnatite.desc:
The de-facto Rare Earth vein for progression in §5EV§r... and onwards.

§l§3Lore:§r§o This vein was bugged for quite some time. It's never actually contained any Monazite, and nobody realised (well, nobody brought it up!) for many, many months. Did you notice?
phoenix_chronicles.quest.emerald.title: Emerald
phoenix_chronicles.quest.emerald.descrip: Emerald is the useful ore here. It's used in small quantities in §bMV§r, and is a part of the Crystal process for Crystal and Wetware circuits much later on.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.molybdenum.desc:
This vein is very rare! Congratulations on stumbling upon one.

§8(Or at least... it should be rare.)§r

View the contents of this vein as "§7§obasically Molybdenum, and some other stuff§r". Yeah, Molybdenum is what's important here.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.certus_quartz.d:
Your ticket into §bApplied Energistics 2§r is nestled deep within a Certus Quartz vein.

Alongside this, note that Barite electrolyses into Barium, which you will eventually need to make some higher tier Superconductors.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.saltpeter.title: Saltpeter
phoenix_chronicles.quest.saltpeter.descr:
Electrotine is important for progression in §6HV§r. It centrifuges into Electrum (a source of Gold and Silver), and Redstone.

Saltpeter is used in a few reactions, and... the other two ores here are pretty average.

---


§l§3Lore:§r§o Does the word "Nikolite" ring a bell? It's pretty much Electrotine's great-ancestor, hailing from RedPower.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.topaz.title: Topaz
phoenix_chronicles.quest.topaz.subtitle: Source of Copper, Fluorine
phoenix_chronicles.quest.topaz.descripti:
Both Topaz ores are excellent subjects for eventual electrolysis.

This makes this vein one of the best Fluorine sources.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.tetrahedrite.de:
Almost a pure Copper vein. Damn you, Stibnite, ruining our purity!

You can hardly complain about its presence, though - Stibnite smelts directly into Antimony, which you will want in §7LV§r for your Batteries.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.limonite_0afa.d:
This Nether Limonite vein variant isn't to be slept on.

Thanks to the §adoubled yield§r of Nether ores, this is an excellent source of Iron and Gold.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.sulfur.title: Sulfur
phoenix_chronicles.quest.sulfur.subtitle: Source of Sulfur, Iron, Zinc
phoenix_chronicles.quest.sulfur.descript:
Your first Nether expedition should be for §eSulfur§r - which is found in this vein! Be careful, as this vein usually spawns from y-levels of 10 to 30. Bring Fire Resistance potions!

Sphalerite is extremely valuable, as its ore processing gives Gallium. It also smelts directly into Zinc.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.quartz.title: Quartz
phoenix_chronicles.quest.quartz.subtitle: Source of Nether Quartz, Silicon
phoenix_chronicles.quest.quartz.descript:
Your classic Nether Quartz vein.

Silicon isn't too difficult to come by, but Quartzite isn't a bad source.
Source of Iron, Vanadium, Gold, Chromium

You may already have boatloads of Iron by the time you make it here, but don't overlook the utility of this vein.

Chromite is an excellent source of Chromium, and Vanadium is needed in higher quantities in the late game.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.naquadah_143b.d:
Seasoned sci-fi fans might recognise §2Naquadah§r from the series §dStargate§r! You'll find this becomes an essential material from §dLuV§r onwards.

Naquadah can be processed in §dLuV§r for Titanium, Trinium, Barium, Gallium, Indium, Phosphorus, Enriched Naquadah, and Naquadria. Versatile!

Moving the spotlight to the other ore, §cPlutonium§r is used to start the Radon loop, required in §9IV§r.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.sheldonite.desc:
Platinum starts seeing usage in §5EV§r.

The Platinum Group Sludge chain becomes a requirement in §1IV§r, and Sheldonite is the best ore to kickstart your processing.

---


§l§3Lore:§r§o The real-world name for Sheldonite ore is actually Cooperite. GregoriusT thought it was "haha, funny" to make it a reference to Sheldon Cooper, despite §lnot§r§o being the person the ore was named after!  We kept the "haha, funny" joke going.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.scheelite.title: Scheelite
phoenix_chronicles.quest.scheelite.descr:
Your one and only §9Tungsten§r source! Whilst you could technically get your Tungstate from macerating §eEnd Stone,§r the yield is tiny. Process these ores instead!

An extremely important vein, as Tungsten is used in vast amounts in §9IV§r and onwards.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.bauxite.title: Bauxite
phoenix_chronicles.quest.bauxite.descrip:
The vein to mine for §bAluminium§r and §dTitanium§r if you're a well-adjusted person.

Ditch those Mica veins - Bauxite is the future!
phoenix_chronicles.quest.pitchblende.des:
The one and only vein for Uranium!

Uranium has a few minor uses in §5EV§r and beyond.

Did you know that Nuclear Reactors might be making their way to §bGTCEu§r in the future?
phoenix_chronicles.quest.high_voltage_ma:
When your power generation allows for it, §3HV machines§r are well worth using for on-demand processing. The quadrupled energy cost compared to their §7LV§r counterparts shouldn't bother you too much.

§9Note:§r Crafting Hulls in the §3Assembler§r is slightly more efficient. Prioritise this recipe!
phoenix_chronicles.quest.super_batteries: §aEnergium Crystals§r store a significant amount of §9EU§r. They're also arguably cheaper.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.hv_autoclave.de:
The §3HV Autoclave§r - despite being optional - is a machine you'll definitively want to grab.

This unlocks unique Batteries that are §6far superior§r to their standard counterparts.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.high_voltage_ba:
The §3HV Chemical Bath§r is used to §ddye Lenses§r using §aChemical Dye§r. This will let you engrave more types of Wafers!

This is also required for §aEyes of Ender§r.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.advanced_mainte:
You now have access to two §3new Maintenance Hatches§r. Both hatches §6do not require Maintenance§r when first placed in a Multiblock. We're going to ask for both here.

The §3Automatic Maintenance Hatch§r is pretty simple - it eliminates the need for Maintenance, §6forever§r.

The §3Configurable Maintenance Hatch§r is more interesting. You can configure it to cut off §a10% duration§r on recipes, at the cost of making Maintenance happen three times as fast. That's §d16 real hours§r of activity.

§9Reminder:§r You can put Tape in the maintenance Hatch to automatically fix problems.

---


§l§3Lore:§r§o The Automatic Maintenance Hatch texture and mechanic comes from TecTech, an addon mod originally made for GregTech: New Horizons.

§oYou'll see more from TecTech if you stick with us all the way to the late game.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.we_call_this_fu:
Just like §bMV§r, you'll need to make higher-tier components.

The painful §dFlawless Gems§r have been replaced with slightly-more-painful §dEyes of Ender§r. Also notice that the §aMotors§r require §d2x Silver Cables§r.

§aHulls§r and §aMachines§r use §dGold Cables§r.

---


§9§lTips to make life less painful:§r

- Consider using §dElectrotine decomposition§r and §dOre Processing§r for §eElectrum§r.
- Consider using the §3Chemical Bath§r with §dMercury§r for §eGold§r from a wide variety of ores.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.hv_assembling_m: The §3HV Assembling Machine§r is the next step in progression, but also unlocks a handful of useful utilities - snoop around this quest for more.
Time to say goodbye to your §4Primitive Water Pumps§r. They've done you proud.

Place this on the side of a machine to give it §616 buckets§o§r§r of Water every second!
phoenix_chronicles.quest.i_see_the_world: I see the world in colour

The §aSimple System on Chip§r will be used for the best §dULV Circuit§r recipe.

We'd also recommend going out of your way to make all the other useful colored Lenses ahead of time. They are listed here in an §eoptional§r task.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.best_ulv_circui: Good on you for making these!
§8ULV§r Circuits are used in some AE2 recipes, such as the §aAnnihilation Core§r and §aFormation Core§r.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.digital_fluid_s:
§bDigital fluid storage§r is pretty cool. Each §b1k ME Fluid Storage Cell§r holds up to §d5 types§r of fluid, and can hold §6over 8,000 buckets§r of those 5 fluid types! That's more than a §3Super Tank 2§r!

You may want to §4format§r Fluid Storage Cells to certain types to prevent the network from clogging. Make a §3Cell Workbench§r to do so.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.upgrade_your_eb:
The §aLow Power Integrated Circuit§r requires an §3HV Cutting Machine§r inside your §3Cleanroom§r.

§3HV Energy Hatches§r will be nice additions so you can run your Multiblocks (mainly your Electric Blast Furnace and Large Chemical Reactor) directly off a §6HV§r line.

You'll need to upgrade your EBF with §32 Energy Hatches§r to obtain §eNichrome coils§r - fun!
phoenix_chronicles.quest.high_voltage_ch:
The §3HV Chemical Reactor§r unlocks a ton of new recipes. Ah, who doesn't love the ever-growing demand on more advanced Chemistry?

§9Note:§r We've actually unlocked a ton of new content by reaching §6HV§r. However, not every processing line or item is crucial right now. It'd make the §6HV§r chapter far too dense if we included everything!

You could still check out the §5EV§r Chapter if you want to push yourself.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.almost_titanium:
Titanium requires a slightly more §binvolved§r process than the previous materials to process. To get started, you'll need §aRutile§r, which can be obtained by processing §aBauxite§r.

Once you've gotten enough §5Rutile§r, your journey to §6Titanium§r continues in the next quest. There's no need to rush things.

---


You may have already noticed that Bauxite is also an §6excellent source of Aluminium§r.

Visiting §dThe End§r allows you to access a richer Bauxite vein, as well as §9Ilmenite§r - an even better source of Rutile.

§9Tip:§r Ore processing for §aBauxite§r is ridiculously good! Including the §3Thermal Centrifuge§r step easily §6triples§r your §aRutile§r yield.

To get your grubby hands on some Titanium, §aRutile§r must first be reduced to §aTitanium Tetrachloride§r in an §3HV Chemical Reactor§r, then reduced again in an §3EBF§r with §dMagnesium§r to finally arrive at Titanium.

The §dCarbon§r, §dChlorine§r, §dOxygen§r, and §dMagnesium§r used in the process can be §6perfectly recovered§r from the byproduct §dCarbon Monoxide§r and §dMagnesium Chloride§r with no loss. If you set up a system to recover them, §athe only material§r that you'll need to provide for Titanium is §dRutile§r!

---


§aTitanium Tetrachloride§r also acts as a catalyst in the production of plastics. A touch of §aTiCl₄§r in the polymerisation process can increase the polymer yield to §6133%§r§r. Naturally, this is completely optional.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.hv_superconduct:
By this point, normal Cables have such insignificant loss that superconductors aren't a requirement.

You can use those as a flex!

Superconductors are still required to craft §aField Generators§r.
phoenix_chronicles.task.hv_superconducto: mercury barium calcium cuprate single wire
A long way to go before we beat the Sun

§3Nichrome Heating Coils§r increase the temperature of your §3Blast Furnace§r to §d3,600K§r.

Despite not being required §oyet§r, it's still a good idea to upgrade your primary §3EBF§r for those sweet, sweet §6Coil bonuses§r.

---


§l§3Lore:§r§o In the original GregTech 5, there were only three types of coils. This was the last tier.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.source_imbued_t:
§5Source Imbued Titanium§r§r has the highest corrosion resistance, magic resistance, and strength-to-density ratio of any metallic element, so it's only natural that it will be used as a base for §5EV§r machinery.

Confirm that your closed loop for §aRutile§r is up to standard, and prepare to run a dedicated §3EBF§r for hours. You also need to get some §5Source§r, which is obtained by running any plant/log through the Alchemical Imbuer multiblock.



---


A quick aside - now we're at §5EV§r, single block generators are about to fall out of style! You'll need to run several §3HV Generators§r to keep up - later, upgrades to Multiblock Generators will be required.

Whilst Multiblock generators are much more expensive, you'll find them to be much more energy efficient!
phoenix_chronicles.quest.300iq.title: 300IQ
phoenix_chronicles.quest.300iq.subtitle: Can we get much smarter? Apparently so
phoenix_chronicles.quest.300iq.descripti:
§oThis is a guide on how to automatically route §lall§r§o your Hot Ingots to your Vacuum Freezer while keeping everything automated perfectly fine.§r

You already know the drill from the Chemical Bath, so let's get right to the chase.

---


Install an §aItem Tag Filter§r Cover on the §3Input Bus§r of your §3Vacuum Freezer§r, open it and set to whitelist §e§lhot_ingots§r. The slot is to §dtest§r items to make sure you configured the Filter properly in case you forgot. Drag ingots from EMI!

From here, you now have the option to route either with §9Item Pipes§r or §9AE2§r.

---


§2With Item Pipes§r, connect the output of your §3EBF(s)§r to the input of your §3Vacuum Freezer§r and the output dump (Chest, Crate, or ME Interface).
You can also have a §dRestrictive Pipe§r in front of the output dump to ensure the Vacuum Freezer will be prioritized.

§2With AE2§r, place a §3ME Storage Bus§r on top of your Cover and set to very §dhigh priority§r. Any hot ingots entering your ME system will automatically be moved into the Vacuum Freezer.

---


§l§9Note:§r If you wish to know more tags for future automation setups, they will display if you press Shift when hovering over an item. For instance, an item tagged with §e§o#forge:plates/copper§r would be filtered as §e§lplates/copper§r.

§9Other Note:§r The Item Tag Filter partially supports §dregex§r. Hover over the info icon for more information.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.ice_cold.title: Ice Cold
phoenix_chronicles.quest.ice_cold.subtit: Did you know vacuums actually make things hotter?
phoenix_chronicles.quest.ice_cold.descri:
The §3Vacuum Freezer§r is a multiblock used to cool down §eHot Ingots§r. All ingots made in the EBF with a temperature above §d1750K§r will need it.

Most of the time, your §3Electric Blast Furnace§r will be the bottleneck, so you don't need to worry about overclocking your freezer.

Since §eHot Ingots§r §churt you§r when held, item routing will be very useful.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.hv_circuit_asse:
The next §3Circuit Assembler§r. This tier of Circuit Assembler is only required for one type of Circuit - your first ever §aMainframe§r.

You can put this off until §5EV§r.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.mainframes_firs:
The first §1IV§r circuit. Congratulations on making it this far!

This will be used when you get to §5EV§r.

§l§3Lore:§r§o The original texture for the Mainframes was taken from an image of an IBM zEnterprise mainframe.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.the_cleanroom.s: They put me in a room... a clean room
phoenix_chronicles.quest.the_cleanroom.d:
The §3Cleanroom§r is a hollow multiblock free of contaminants. Going forward, most new §acircuit-related recipes§r, as well as some unique blocks like §3Fusion Casings§r, will need to be run in machines inside a Cleanroom.

Creating it will put your §aPolyethylene§r automation to the test for all the §dPlascrete§r and/or §dCleanroom Glass§r you will make.

We'll start you off with a 5x5x5 Cleanroom, but you should upgrade its size when you start feeling cramped.

§6This quest unlocks a new tutorial on the Cleanroom in the §lTips and Tricks§r§6 tab - check it out to learn more!§r

---


§l§3Lore:§r§o The Cleanroom comes from GregTech 5, but as is often the case, the GT5 implementation is much more punishing. The recipes would run without regard to cleanliness, but had a % chance of completion equal to the cleanliness of the Cleanroom. This caused a lot of accidental voiding.

§oFurthermore, if the Cleanroom had a maintenance issue, the cleanliness would cap out at 90%, which means 10% of items would be voided.

§oThe GTCEu Cleanroom will §6never void§f recipe outputs.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.fluorine.title: Fluorine
phoenix_chronicles.quest.fluorine.descri:
Fluorine is the rarest gas to obtain from electrolysis in this game.

You can obtain it from §aLepidolite§r, §aBastnatite§r, and §aMica§r, but the best source is from §aTopaz§r.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.polytetrafluoro:
§aPolytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE)§r is a §7Carbon§r-§bFluorine§r polymer. Similarly to PVC, PTFE can be used to increase the yield of Plastic Circuit Boards and other crafts. Presently, it is used to make the walls of §3Large Chemical Reactors§r.

§3Chlorine§r is required in the process, which is fully recycled if you electrolyze the §aHydrochloric Acid§r waste.

§bFluorine§r will also be used in the §aUranium§r and §7Naquadah§r refinement processes.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.benzene_nitro.s: Click this link for free Nitro
phoenix_chronicles.quest.benzene_nitro.d:
Making §aNitrobenzene§r will boost the energy efficiency of §aBenzene§r roughly §6fourfold§r. You love to see it.

The catch here is that it takes §dDistilled Water§r, and consumes a bit of §dSulfur§r with every step.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.large_chemical_: The Magic Box to end all Magic Boxes

The §3Large Chemical Reactor (LCR)§r is a multiblock §3Chemical Reactor§r with more input/output slots. Its Teflon casings allow it to process extra recipes.

The §3LCR§r can perform some exclusive reactions which allow you to combine multiple normal §3Chemical Reactor§r steps into a §6single step§r. Examples below:

§9-§r §aNitrogen Dioxide§r (for Nitric Acid and Dinitrogen Tetroxide)
§9-§r §aSulfuric Acid§r
§9-§r §aPhenol§r
§9-§r §aEpichlorohydrin§r (you need it for Epoxy!)
§9-§r §aEpoxy§r

---


There are also §3LCR§r exclusive recipes. For example, §dRadon§r can only be made in the LCR right now.

All §dOverclocks§r in the §3LCR§r are §6100% efficient§r (known as Perfect overclocks); each overclock will §5quadruple the speed§r, as opposed to doubling it.

The §3LCR§r has yet another §6advantage§r. You can use §32 Energy Hatches§r to allow it to run recipes of the §5next tier§r, similar to the §3Electric Blast Furnace§r.

---


§9Tip:§r Given the amount of LCRs you may end up using, why not try utilising §dwallsharing§r to its full potential?

You could share one 2A (standard) §3Energy Hatch§r between 2 LCRs.

You might want to share §3Input/Output Hatches§r, but make sure each LCR is running the correct recipe.

Keep in mind Maintenance hatches cannot wallshare.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.phosphorus_boul:
Doping is the process of intentionally introducing impurities into semiconductors to alter their properties.

§7Silicon§r can be doped with small amounts of §ePhosphorus§r to make a better §eSilicon Boule§r.

Phosphorus-doped Silicon Boules typically yield §68 times§r more wafers than their non-doped counterparts. However, they are not strictly needed until §5EV§r, where they'll be used in more complex wafers.

§9Note§r: All processing of Phosphorus Boules and Wafers will require a §dCleanroom§r.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.nitric_acid.des:
Nitric Acid's fumes are extremely toxic! It's also a very potent oxidizer.

§aNitric Acid§r is used in:

§9-§r Cetane-Boosted Diesel, a better Diesel fuel that you'll get to soon.
§9-§r Nitrobenzene, a better Gas fuel that we're not far off making.
§9-§r The optional gem slurry chains.
§9-§r The Platinum Group Sludge chain in §1IV§r.
§9-§r Polybenzimidazole (try saying that ten times fast!) in §1IV§r.

---


There are two main ways to make §aNitric Acid§r - §othe §agood§f way and the §4bad§f ways!§r

Therefore, we'll point you towards the best method:

Get a §3Large Chemical Reactor§r and use it to make §aNitrogen Dioxide§r. From there, react it in a regular §3Chemical Reactor§r with more §dOxygen§r and §dWater§r and you got yourself some §aNitric Acid§r!

This requires a lot of §dOxygen§r. Refer to its own Quest in §7LV§r for the most efficient ways to obtain in large amount. Notice that this is Hydrogen free!
phoenix_chronicles.quest.cetaneboosted_d: This is to go further beyond

§aCetane-Boosted Diesel§r is §650% more energy dense§r than regular §aDiesel§r, and only requires 1 part §dTetranitromethane (TNM)§r for every 50 parts §aDiesel§r. What a steal, right?

The catch comes in the complexity of making §dTNM§r. In order to concoct it, you must react §aNitric Acid§r with either §dEthenone§r or §aMethyl Acetate§r, both of which have quite an involved process themselves!
The §eSMD§r (surface-mount device) §aComponents§r are CEu-exclusive components that are required for the next tier of circuits (§5Nano§r). They can also be used in place of their non-SMD counterparts in most Circuit recipes.

Of course they're more complicated to make, this is GregTech! What did you expect?

Invest in automation for these - you won't stop needing them.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.more_smd_compon:
§aPlatinum§r (needed for SMD Diodes) has its own dedicated Quest in the §5EV§r tab.

§l§3Lore:§r§o The SMD Inductors make an appearance in GTCEu for the first time. It's more consistent and convenient to have all Circuit components receive an SMD counterpart.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.universal_macer:
The §3HV Macerator§r finally unlocks more of the slots shown in EMI. With this, the first §9three§r slots are now available. This allows you to receive the §6unique ore Byproduct§r from macerating §dThermal §dCentrifuged Ore§r.

Macerating Ores costs §a32 EU/t§r with §5two overclocks§r, which makes this machine able to fit in §7LV§r lines - very, very convenient.

Despite the signicant improvements this machine provides, it still isn't completely worth it to set up advanced processing for every single ore. Energy and time are still things to consider, so only process the ores that produce §6Byproducts§r you care for.

---


§l§3Lore:§r§o In GregTech 5u, the §6HV§r§o Macerator only gave two slots. Urgh... we weren't planning on using that Stone Dust, anyway...
phoenix_chronicles.quest.ammonia.title: Ammonia
phoenix_chronicles.quest.ammonia.descrip:
§aAmmonia§r is §doptional§r in §6HV§r.

You may use it in the production of:

§9-§r Nitric Acid, although we don't recommend this.

§9-§r Rocket Fuel, required for Nether Stars in §1IV§r.

§9-§r Polybenzimidazole (now THAT'S a tongue twister!) in §1IV§r.

The "least painful" recipe should be the one in the §3HV Chemical Reactor§r. Make sure your §aHydrogen§r production (mostly from §aWater electrolysis§r) is enough to support the demand.

You could also obtain §aAmmonia§r as a waste product from §dPlatinum Group Sludge§r processing.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.void_dimension_:
If you're looking for a change of scene, the §5Void Dimension§r is a perfectly empty area for you to build your factory.

It wouldn't be unwise to procure some manner of §aflight§r before venturing here - maybe look around and see if this pack has §6any options§r.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.nanomuscles_son: GregTech and armour - a match made in heaven!

§9Helmet:§r Provides §dNight vision§r (the default keybind is §4M§r, but check for conflicts)

§9Chestplate:§r Provides nothing interesting right now, but can be further upgraded into the §aAdvanced§r version at the very end of §6HV§r.

§9Leggings:§r Provides nothing special... perhaps we should have given it a small speed boost?

§9Boots:§r Provides §dStep Assist§r. Yes, you read that right!

---


§l§3Lore:§r§o This armor was inspired by IndustrialCraft, but its first implementation within the "GTCE ecosystem" came with Nuke Powered Utils, an addon mod to GTCE.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.dense_coprocess:
With §5EV Circuits§r, you can compress your Coprocessors into §3Dense§r variants to get more value-for-money.

The crafting ratio is in your favour, so you'll likely have more §eparallel autocrafting power§r than you'd need to finish the pack.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.q_76681efd9b76f:
Unlock the power of §5Source!§r In an §eAlchemical Imbuer§r (set to §6Source Extraction Mode§r), process §oplants, fuels, or lava§r to obtain this wonderful resource. You can also use the vitalic sourcelink (baby growth ticks) to generate source. However this is less effecient than using the §eAlchemical Imbuer§r.

Your first step is making §5Source-Imbued Titanium§r. (Also used for the §dev superconductor§r but we will see that later).
phoenix_chronicles.quest.q_79333ae8a6745:
These are the solid manifestation of §bSource§r (obtained through the §9imbuement chamber§r§r block), and they store a great deal of §5magical energy§r. You'll use them to build the §6Alchemical Imbuer§r multiblock and, later on, the §6EV tier superconductor source titanium filaments§r.

When crafting §9Source Gems§r, you have a choice: either cycle some of your §bSource§r back into the imbuer to create these gems §amuch faster§r, or produce them without additional source at a §csignificantly slower rate§r.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.q_2d6f0875cc953:
This is your primary multiblock for handling all §5magical processes§r. Initially, its main purpose is to craft §9Source Gems§r and §5Source Imbued Titanium§r. Later in your journey, this very machine will be essential for cooling a §cvery special metal§r.

To construct this vital multiblock, you'll need unique materials from §aArs Nouveau§r, such as the §aArcane Core§r. These aren't overly difficult to acquire. We highly recommend exploring §aArs Nouveau§r; its power will prove invaluable throughout your journey. As a tip, one of the most delightful uses of its spellbook is the creation of §bMagelights§r, which you can even customize with your preferred color!


---



"Through your time reclaiming the lost §cPhoenix Technologies§r you've learned that it's more than just §btechnology§r needed. It's also §5magic§r. You learn about an old source of power called §aArs Nouveau§r. Designed around the power of ironically §bSource§r you develop a machine to harness this power. You create an §6Imbuer§r that manipulates §bSource§r to push into resources to create new and improved items."
phoenix_chronicles.quest.q_2892d18ffd789:
You will need a lot of §dAmethyst§r for your §9Source Gems§r as you go on. Not to worry though! You can use the §aAE2 Growth Accelerators§r on §5Budding Amethyst§r to grow it quite quickly.

If you are worried about being able to get Budding Amethyst, don't worry! You can take §316 Amethyst Blocks§r and then compress them into a §5Budding Amethyst§r version. This ensures a steady supply for your progression.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.q_70fc1ff864dab:
The §ePressurized Fission Reactor§r stands ready to provide immense power for your operations. Fuel it with §aUranium Oxide Fuel Rods§r to generate a significant output of energy. Do remember to manage those §bcoolers§r thou, you don't want to §o§close everything§r§r because you ran §4out§r.

As a byproduct of its operation, this reactor produces §8waste§r. You can then centrifuge the dust to recover valuable §7Lead§r and §7Thorium§r.

Construct the reactor's robust casings using the §bZircalloy§r you previously obtained. The process gives off §e4 HV amps§r (you will need at least §e2 HV Dynamos§r to handle this power!).



---


"§f§lNecessity is the mother of invention.§r You've learned this throughout the ages, and now, once again, you face its truth. You scan your progress, seeking the §cbottleneck§r, the very thing holding you back. Your gaze settles on your §bpower supply§r, and you decide it's time for a crucial §aupgrade§r.

You uncover an §7old design§r from the §7lost ages§r: a reactor. It's not super efficient, but it will §asuffice§r. You note its reliance on an §cinefficient method of fission§r to generate power, yet your current materials aren't §cstrong enough§r. Then, it clicks: §bZircalloy§r!

Being a §anear-perfect choice§r, you decide to use it. This allows you to almost §aflawlessly sustain fission without damage§r. A §eproud smile§r touches your lips as you survey all you've accomplished. You're §eready, even excited§r, to have survived this long and come this far in §6reclaiming what was once lost§r."
phoenix_chronicles.quest.q_7cb0b82b219b7:
§bZircalloy§r, a crucial alloy, is a precise mixture of §3zirconium§r and §3hafnium dust§r. Its unique properties make it highly §aresistant to extreme heat and fissile reactions§r.

You'll obtain these essential dusts by §acentrifuging zircon dust§r. And where does zircon dust come from? By §acentrifuging blackstone dust§r.

To efficiently acquire blackstone, it's highly recommended you utilize your §eHV Rock Crusher§r; it's perfect for automating this process and ensuring a steady supply!
phoenix_chronicles.quest.q_06f2deb21e1a7:
These §aspecialized fuel rods§r are for your §ePressurized Fission Reactor§r. Designed for §9longevity§r, they'll make generating §bHV power§r a much §asmoother process§r.

Crafting them is §fstraightforward§r: simply §3can§r an §7empty fuel rod§r with §6uranium oxide§r. After that, enjoy your power but manage those risks carefully.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.q_6fd5c824c3b24: Your §efirst fuel§r for fission has arrived! Obtain this wonderful fuel by §3reacting urananite dust with oxygen§r.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.moderators_and_: Man, I thought fission was going to be simple.

Along with the §abase structure§r and the §afuel§r for your §2fission reactors§r, you also need §afission§r §6moderators§r and §bcoolers§r. The §cexplosion strength§r is decided by the tier of §bcooler§r you use. As they say, §chigh risk§r:§6high reward§r.

§bCoolers§r: These are §o§cnecessary§r§r to make sure your reactor doesn't §4§lblow up§r§r. These have a §3linear progression§r of tiers. Higher tier coolers are needed for higher tier recipes, so §o§cmake sure§r§r that you check §aemi§r before you start. Each cooler has it's own §bcoolant§r and §3cooling power§r so you'll need a few to meet the recipe's need. Moreover, each cooler block shows you the relevant info on shift.

Your first cooler is aptly named, §bBasic Cooler§r. Good luck and don't blame me if your base has an §l§cexplosive suprise§r§r!



---



§6Moderators§r: These are §o§cnecessary§r§r to form your reactors and they provide some §6beautiful benefits§r. Each §6moderator§r has it's own §aEU Boost§r (power generation bonus) and §9Fuel Discount§r (recipe duration bonus). Unlike §bcoolers§r, the reactors §o§adon't really care§r§r what §6moderator§r it has. You can mix and match §6moderators§r, go crazy!

Your first §6moderator§r is the graphite moderator. With a §aEU Boost§r of §61%§r and §9Fuel Discount§r of §61%§r per block, this moderator will provide a delightful base for your future fissile goals.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.source_logistic: Heard ya wanted to learn magic.

Your way of using §dArs Nouveau§r §5Source§r in GregTech multiblocks. To move §5Source§r long distances you will want to use §5Source§r jars and §5Source§r relays, with the source hatches acting as §aendpoints§r. The distance that jars can be seen by a §5Source§r hatch is by default §a12 blocks§r, anything longer than that will require your §dWand Of Dominion§r.

§5Source§r Input: Used by the Alchemical Imbuer and §5Source§r Reactor to transform §2mundane§r resources into more §dmagical§r variants.

§5Source§r Output: Used by the Alchemical Imbuer's §5Source§r Extraction Mode to provide you source through carbon based materials.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.q_5cf27689e362a: Telling your magic what to do.

This is your §atool§r to control long-distance §5Source§r lines, it handles connection between one source transmitter and one source receiver.

§5Source§r Jar to §5Source§r Relay: Right click on the jar to set it as the §atransmitter§r, and right click on the relay to set it as the §6receiver§r.

§5Source§r Relay to §5Source§r Jar: Right click on the relay to set it as the §atransmitter§r, and right click on the jar to set it as the §6receiver§r.

After you mess around with it for a bit, try setting up a real set of §5Source§r §alogistics§r linking up all your §dmagical§r infrastructure.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.large_steam_tur: If you're still running off Steam... boy, do we have a solution for you!

It's time to be blunt - Steam as a power option isn't gonna cut the mustard anymore. If you're going to stick with Steam until the bitter end, we wish you luck... so read on.

The §3Large Steam Turbine§r acts as a multiblock Steam Turbine for §6HV§r power. It's quite an expensive multiblock to build just for a measly 1024 EU/t, but it also boasts the powerful ability to scale to §9higher power production and higher efficiency§r.

§8(We're trying our best to sell it here, okay?!)

---


The Turbine outputs §dDistilled Water§r if given an §3Output Hatch§r, which you could loop back to your §3Large Boilers§r. We don't entirely endorse this, as your Boilers could end up exploding if this system fails.

Each Large Turbine will require a §aTurbine Rotor§r and a §3Rotor Holder§r. You can find out more about the Turbine mechanics in the §lnext§r Quest.

---


§9Note:§r This Quest §eonly§r requires the Controller, but you'll still need all the multiblock parts to construct the Turbine.

Turbines §cvoid§r energy if they're unable to output. If you plan on using this with §6HV§r power, use a Rotor close to a 100% Power stat.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.large_turbine_m:
The Large Turbines are the most complex Multiblock Generators that you'll find in GTCEu in the present day.

Let's delve into Turbines!

§6This quest unlocks a new tutorial on Turbine Mechanics in the §lTips and Tricks§r§6 tab - check it out to learn more!§r
phoenix_chronicles.quest.upgrading_your_:
Starting from here, §3Energy§r and §3Dynamo Hatches§r can be upgraded to a §d4A§r variant.

This is extremely useful for Multiblock generators, or boosting your GCYM machinery.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.large_gas_turbi:
The §3Large Gas Turbine§r may not impress you in §5EV§r, but it can scale to §9better production§r than the base 4096 EU/t, and boasts §9higher efficiency§r than those pesky singleblock generators.

Each Large Turbine will require a §aTurbine Rotor§r and a §3Rotor Holder§r. More on the Turbine mechanics in the §lnext§r Quest.

---


§9Note:§r This Quest §eonly§r requires the Controller, but obviously you still need all the multiblock parts to construct the Turbine.

Turbines §cvoid§r energy if they're unable to output. If you plan on using this with HV power, use a Rotor with close to 100% Power stat.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.power_integrate: No one machine should have all this power!

So, what's on the agenda today?

New Cutting Machine? §a✓§r

New Lens? §a✓§r

New Power Circuit? §a✓§r

New EBF Metal required? §a✓§r

New Coil for Energy Hatch? §a✓§r

§9Note:§r If you haven't found a Jungle yet, you can §acentrifuge Stone Dust§r for §dMetal Mixture Dust§r. This doubles as a Brown Dye.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.large_combustio:
The §3Large Combustion Engine§r is a multiblock that can burn §dCombustion Fuels§r for even... more... power generation!

By default, this puppy outputs 2048 EU/t, which is equivalent to 4 §3Turbo Combustion Generators§r.

This might not convince you, but unlike the singleblock generators, you can actually §6boost this§r by providing §aOxygen§r. This will §cdouble§r the fuel consumption, but §atriple§r the power generation. This'll output 6144 EU/t with §6150% Fuel efficiency§r.

You'll also need to supply a small amount of §aLubricant§r to the LCE during operation - nothing too crazy.

---


The §3LCE§r is also void-free, unlike Large Turbines. Any energy that cannot be output will momentarily pause the multiblock.

To harness the cataclysmic power of the 6144 EU/t output, you'll need a §34A EV Dynamo Hatch§r or an §3IV Dynamo Hatch§r.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.extreme_fluid_d:
At the cost of 4x the drilling Power, the §3Advanced Fluid Drilling Rig§r gains §616x the output§r in Fluid.

The depletion of veins is also halved. This means you will get a total of §632x§r as much Oil (or whatever fluid) from a bedrock fluid vein until depletion!

Even when depleted, you can still use this and be firmly power positive.

One single §3Advanced Fluid Drilling Rig§r should be enough to supply Power for a base up to §dLuV§r... and possibly beyond!

---


As a §9reminder§r, since this last appeared in §bMV§r:

§9-§r §aLight Oil§r can be used for §dLPG§r and §dMethane§r to run in §3Large Gas Turbines§r.
§9-§r §aOil§r can be used for §dDiesel§r and §dCetane-Boosted Diesel§r to run in §3Large Combustion Engines§r.
§9-§r §aHeavy Oil§r can be used for §dNitrobenzene§r to run in §3Large Gas Turbines§r.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.platinum.title: Platinum
phoenix_chronicles.quest.platinum.descri:
How do you get Platinum?

§9-§r As a byproduct of §aNickel Ore§r processing, either with a §3Chemical Bath§r, or a §3HV Macerator§r
§9-§r From §aSheldonite veins§r in the End
§9-§r From §aPlatinum Group Sludge§r, a complicated chain granting all Platinum Group metals. Highly §cunrecommended until IV§r, but eventually required.

Platinum is needed in small amounts for §dSMD Diodes§r, and for a plethora of recipes starting in §5EV§r.

---


§l§3Lore:§r§o Mekanism's primary material was planned to be Platinum. However, GregoriusT didn't agree - the fact that such a rare material could be found all over the world wasn't quite to his tastes. The Mekanism devs thus opted to make the primary material Osmium.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.multiblock_mine:
Yeah, we admit it... this Multiblock is entirely §doptional§r. Many playtesters kept using their §6HV§r singleblock miners and didn't run into any issues with regards to throughput.

However, the §3Large Miner§r will further boost your returns when collecting ores from veins. Ores are mined as if they were §amacerated§r, but they yield §6three times§r as many §dCrushed ores§r.

You'll need to automate §aDrilling Fluid§r before you run this. You might also want to use a §3Quantum Tunnel§r from AE2 and §3GTEU P2P Tunnels§r to transfer items and provide power.

---


§l§3Lore:§r§o There were some interesting side effects when we ported this over from Gregicality, as the multiblock actually originated from GregTech 5.

§oIts current implementation isn't perfect, as you don't really get much of a benefit by upgrading this miner to the advanced versions. We were considering a rebalance of energy consumption and yield per tier.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.ev_assembler.de: You know the drill by now. It's an Assembler - what else do you need to know?
phoenix_chronicles.quest.extreme_batteri:
The best battery-like item for §5EV§r!

Making a §aLapotron Crystal§r will require quite a bit of nested crafting, so craft these in large batches - or, of course, automate everything with §bAE2§r patterns.
This quest will cover the Tungsten Chain. §aTungsten§r is obtained from either §eTungstate§r or §eScheelite§r, which are part of the same vein in the End.

Just like the §dRutile§r chain, you will only need to input one item type, and everything else will be looped perfectly!

---


You will need:

§9-§r One §3Chemical Bath§r, to make §dTungstic Acid§r.
§9-§r One §3Electrolyzer§r, to electrolyze §oboth§r Bath outputs.
§9-§r One §3Chemical Reactor§r, to loop §dHydrogen§r and §dChlorine§r back into §aHydrochloric Acid§r.

You will be granted either Calcium or Lithium as a byproduct - it's on the house!

---


§l§3Lore:§r§o In GTCE, Tungstate or Scheelite took 40sec and 4,000mB of Hydrogen @ 1920 EU/t to electrolyze into 1 Tungsten Dust. Even if it was simpler, it was much more expensive!
The §3EV Mixer§r is required for more alloys.

This is important if you want to get your hands on some §dTungstensteel§r.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.voidium_touched:
This advanced alloy, §bVoidium Touched Tungsten Steel§r, commands respect with its complex composition. You'll produce its dust by mixing §5liquid ender air§r, §32 Vanadium Steel Dust§r, §34 Tungsten Dust§r, and §34 Voidglass Shard Dust§r. Once mixed, this dust will need to be smelted into its final form.

Right now, it's a crucial ingredient for §3Energy§r or §3Dynamo Hatches§r, bringing you one step closer to moving beyond those pesky single-block Generators!

Boosting the §eElectric Blast Furnace§r smelting of this dust will require §eHelium§r. You can get an initial supply from §aextracting Monazite§r or §acentrifuging Endstone§r. In the long term, you will want to get Helium via §aLiquid Air Distillation§r.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.tungsten.title: Tungsten
phoenix_chronicles.quest.tungsten.descri:
Tungsten in Swedish translates directly as "Heavy Stone", which is pretty funny. You may know of this element as Wolfram too, hence its formula being W.

§aTungsten§r will be the main §1IV§r Cable material, but will also show its face elsewhere!
phoenix_chronicles.quest.p2p_tunnels.des:
Even without channels, P2P Tunnels are still extremely important automation tools!

§9Note:§r There are many fantastic resources online to explain how P2P Tunnels work. The short description is that they allow transfer of things from 1 input to endless output. You can link them using a Memory Card.

This Quest acts as a tutorial on how to use the P2P Tunnels to your own benefit.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.gregicality_mul:
If you want a big boost to your processing abilities, look no further than these powerful Multiblocks!

Formerly known as §2Gregicality Multiblocks§r, the add-on has been fully integrated into GregTech CEu Modern!

You'll need to make use of many new §9alloys§r to build the new Multiblocks. Yay, more content!

§6This quest unlocks a new tutorial on the GCYM mechanics in the §lTips and Tricks§r§6 tab - check it out to learn more!§r
phoenix_chronicles.quest.rtm_alloy_coils:
§aRTM Alloy Coils§r raise the Heat Capacity to a scorching §d4,500K§r.

These will be required in §9IV§r, but as always, you should get them earlier for the §6Coil bonuses§r.

§l§3Lore:§r§o These coils used to be Tungstensteel Coils. This however made most of the EV tier very easy to skip over and postpone to IV, so they were changed to the new RTM Alloy. GTNH was the first to make this change, and used TPV Alloy instead, made from Titanium, Platinum, and Vanadium.

§o§7Which coil do you prefer?
phoenix_chronicles.quest.diode.title: Diode
phoenix_chronicles.quest.diode.descripti:
The §3Diode§r (the block, not the component) accepts energy inputs from 5 sides, but only outputs through a single side.

Its main purpose is to §dlimit Amperage§r. It'll help you regulate any centralised power generation, so you can distribute your power everywhere without having to math out what cable size is safe depending on consumers...

They can also be used as an electric equivalent to Repeaters when the voltage loss from Cables (or GTEU P2P tunnels - more on that later!) gets too high.

You can use a §5Soft Hammer§r to change the Amperage limit of the output.

§eAny§r of the listed Diodes will complete this Quest.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.the_fun_will_ne:
A lot of §dKanthal§r will be required for the §aEV Motors§r. This may feel painful when you're on the edge of §5EV§r, but it won't be a problem later - trust us.

§dNeodymium§r is the metal used for §aMagnetic Rods§r.

§aAluminium Cables§r require §dPVC§r to be insulated.

Lastly, you will need §4Radon§r for the §dQuantum Eyes§r in the §aEmitter§r recipe.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.me_hatches.desc:
§3ME Hatches§r directly connect to your §aAE System§r, allowing you to skip placing interfaces directly on buses and hatches.

§l§3Lore:§r§o This feature originally comes from GTNH!
phoenix_chronicles.quest.even_more_bypro: Avarice and hedonism in a single block

You've probably noticed the §9"chance per tier"§r when hovering over the bonus outputs in §2EMI§r in previous versions.

However, with the §l§cremoval of chance boosting§r§r in the §oGTM 7.x§r versions, macerators beyond hv only have the use of faster recipe times.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.ev_circuit_asse:
Quite a journey to get here.

The §3EV Circuit Assembling§r "unlocks" the next tier of Circuits, §5Nano§r.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.extreme_chemica:
Note that in theory, the §3EV Chemical Reactor§r is skippable by using the §3Large Chemical Reactor§r instead, but we're evil enough to force you to make this.

§7It's still useful due to its compact size!

§8Honestly, if making one of these is a huge problem material-wise, take a look at your infrastructure.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.nano_cpus.title: Nano CPUs
phoenix_chronicles.quest.nano_cpus.descr:
§aNano CPU Wafers§r are made by infusing regular §aCPU Wafers§r with §dGlowstone§r and §9Raw Carbon Fibers§r.

They will be needed in large quantities when making the §5Nano§r line of Circuits.

Higher-tier polymers will increase your yield of §9Raw Carbon Fibers§r. One §dEpoxy§r is enough for a full stack.

§9Tip:§r Don't like mining §dGlowstone§r? Check out Redstone ore processing.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.best_hv_circuit:
Making the best §6HV§r Circuits will allow for easier §6HV§r Machines for your on-demand automation. Convenient!

Starting from here, all circuit lines will be consistent with each other until the end of the game.

Each tier until §cZPM§r will show its own challenges when acquiring new and better Circuits.
phoenix_chronicles.quest.advanced_circui:
